jobs.title: Senior AI Software Engineer
jobs.description:
At NiCE, we don’t limit our challenges. We challenge our limits. Always. We’re ambitious. We’re game changers. And we play to win. We set the highest standards and execute beyond them. And if you’re like us, we can offer you the ultimate career opportunity that will light a fire within you.

The team

NiCE Labs (nice.com/nice-labs) is where NiCE explores what's next in AI for customer experience. This role is on AI Innovation, the Labs pillar that builds and validates new AI capabilities through prototypes, so the company can make better product decisions, faster. 

We're a deliberately small, senior team of builders inside NiCE Cognigy, the AI agent platform. We operate in fast iteration cycles: spot an emerging capability, build a working prototype, validate it against real metrics (quality, latency, cost, user impact), and then decide: kill it, iterate, publish it, or hand it off to a product team. Some of our work is public, like the open-sourced Cognigy Platform MCP server; most of it shapes the product roadmap from the inside. 

We hire for product mindset and builder mentality. Everyone on the team takes ideas from zero to working software, shows them to real users, and argues from evidence. 

So, what’s the role all about?

You'll work at the intersection of frontier AI capabilities and a real enterprise product. The field moves faster than any roadmap can track. Your job is to close that gap: turn new models, protocols, and agent patterns into working systems, prove what matters in realistic scenarios, and produce the insights and reference implementations that let product and engineering teams move with confidence. 

You'll need to be comfortable with ambiguity, at home where best practices don't exist yet, and quick to move on when the results point elsewhere. 

How will you make an impact?  

  • Build agentic systems and full-stack prototypes end-to-end, shipping a first version in days and learning from real use
  • Track the frontier (new models, agent patterns, protocols like MCP) and turn the promising ones into working prototypes rather than slideware
  • Design experiments that show whether a concept holds up, measured in quality, latency, cost, and user impact
  • Work directly with internal users, product managers, and customers to validate concepts early and iterate quickly 
  • Turn validated prototypes into reference implementations and write-ups that product teams can build on, then hand off cleanly and move to the next bet
  • Give product and platform teams concrete feedback on where AI capabilities shine and where they fall short
  • Move between initiatives as priorities shift. What you learn on one bet compounds into the next

Have you got what it takes?

  • Have 4+ years building full-stack software, including things you started from nothing. We weigh what you've shipped more than years on a CV 
  • Have shipped LLM-powered systems to production:features real users depended on, not demos or notebooks 
  • Understand AI agents below the framework level: message arrays, tool calling, context management, prompt caching. You could build an agent loop from scratch and explain why it works
  • Use AI-assisted development (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or similar) as your default way of working, and it makes you measurably faster, not just busier
  • Are full-stackin practice: comfortable taking a prototype from API to demo UI on your own (our stack centers on TypeScript/Node.js and React) 
  • Do your best work when the ground is still moving. New territory energises you more than a settled plan
  • Think in user problems first, solutions second

You will have an advantage if you also have:

  • A strong eye for UX/UI: you can make a prototype feel like a product, and you notice when one lacks that eye
  • Experience with voice and real-time AI: streaming, speech-to-text/text-to-speech, voice-to-voice models
  • Open-source work on agent tooling (MCP servers, harnesses, evals)
  • Experience designing evaluations for AI systems
  • Background in conversational AI or customer-experience products

Enjoy NICE-FLEX!  

At NICE, we work according to the NICE-FLEX hybrid model, which enables maximum flexibility: 2 days working from the office and 3 days of remote work, each week. Naturally, office days focus on face-to-face meetings, where teamwork and collaborative thinking generate innovation, new ideas, and a vibrant, interactive atmosphere.

jobs.title: Senior DevOps Engineer
jobs.description:
About the role

0G is hiring its first dedicated DevOps engineer to own our cloud platform end to end: infrastructure, deployments, networking, security hygiene and cost. Today that work is spread across several developers.

Our platform runs on five providers: Google Cloud, Alibaba Cloud, AWS, Cloudflare and Vercel. It includes:

• 
Validator, seed, RPC, and archive nodes for our mainnet and testnet

• 
Confidential-computing (TEE) workloads, GPU machines and storage nodes

• 
Kubernetes clusters and managed databases

• 
A global RPC load balancer at the edge, and our web apps

All together, that is more than 200 virtual machines. You will be the person who knows what runs where, why it runs there, and what it costs.

What you'll own

You own the platform, from the network edge to the bill.

• 
Cloud operations: provisioning, upgrades, capacity and the full resource lifecycle on Google Cloud, Alibaba Cloud and AWS. That includes rightsizing and releasing what nobody uses.

• 
Kubernetes: run, upgrade and scale our clusters. Keep them on supported versions and design node pools, autoscaling and Spot capacity.

• 
Blockchain node fleet: operate validator, sentry, seed, RPC and archive nodes, including peering topology, snapshots, sync and client upgrades.

• 
Networking and edge: VPC design, load balancers, DNS, Cloudflare Workers, Tunnels and WAF, and keeping internet egress deliberate and cheap.

• 
Infrastructure as code and CI/CD: every environment defined in Terraform or Pulumi. You design and run CI/CD on Jenkins or an equivalent such as GitHub Actions or GitLab CI, covering builds, tests, security scans and releases from commit to production, with no manual steps.

• 
Observability and on-call: metrics, logs, alerts and dashboards, including control of metric cardinality. You also run incident response and write the postmortems.

• 
Security and access: least-privilege IAM across every provider, secrets management, and no databases or admin ports open to the internet.

• 
Cost management: billing exports, budgets and alerts, tagging, a monthly cost review and commitment planning.

• 
Developer enablement: templates, preview environments, documentation and support for the engineers who ship on the platform.

Our stack

Kubernetes: GKE, EKS, Helm, Ingress and Gateway API, autoscaling, RBAC, network policies

Networking: TCP/IP, subnets and CIDR, routing, NAT, L4 and L7 load balancers, DNS, TLS, firewalls, VPC peering

Google Cloud: Compute Engine, GKE, Cloud SQL, Cloud Run, IAM, Cloud Monitoring, billing export to BigQuery

Infrastructure as code: Terraform, Pulumi

CI/CD and containers: Jenkins or an equivalent (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI), Argo CD, Docker and BuildKit, container registries

Observability: Prometheus, Grafana, Cloud Monitoring, CloudWatch, Alibaba CloudMonitor

Linux: Systems administration, systemd, disks and filesystems, performance debugging

Alibaba Cloud: ECS, VPC, NLB and ALB, ESSD disks, RDS, PolarDB, SAE, Cloud Firewall

AWS: EC2, EKS, RDS, ALB and NLB, Route 53, S3, Organizations

Cloudflare: DNS, Workers, Tunnels, WAF and rate limiting, Zero Trust

Databases (operations): PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, managed Kafka

Blockchain nodes: CometBFT-based chains, reth and other EVM clients, P2P networking

Vercel: Projects, builds, ISR, team access

Confidential computing: Intel TDX virtual machines on Google Cloud and Alibaba Cloud

Must-haves

• 
We want 5+ years in DevOps, SRE or platform roles, including 3+ years running production Kubernetes and owning CI/CD pipelines.

Kubernetes, in depth

• 
Upgrading control planes and node pools with no downtime, and keeping clusters on supported versions.

• 
Scheduling: requests and limits, affinity, taints and tolerations, priority, and eviction under node pressure.

• 
Autoscaling with the HPA, cluster autoscaler or Karpenter, plus Spot or preemptible node pools for non-critical work.

• 
Networking inside the cluster: CNI, Services, Ingress or Gateway API, network policies, and DNS within the cluster.

• 
Security: RBAC, Pod Security, workload identity, and secrets that never sit in plain environment variables.

• 
Stateful workloads: StatefulSets, persistent volumes and CSI drivers, and backup and restore.

• 
Packaging and delivery with Helm or Kustomize, ideally through GitOps with Argo CD or Flux.

• 
Debugging a failing pod, node or rollout from events, logs and metrics.

CI/CD, in depth

• 
Pipeline design: you have built and run production CI/CD on Jenkins or an equivalent (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, CircleCI, Tekton). Pipelines are defined as code in a Jenkinsfile or workflow YAML, with shared libraries and reusable templates.

• 
CI platform operations: running Jenkins controllers with ephemeral agents on Kubernetes, or self-hosted runners. That includes plugin and version upgrades, credential handling, and scaling build capacity.

• 
Build pipelines: multi-service and monorepo builds with caching and parallel stages, and versioned artifacts. Container images built with Docker, BuildKit or Kaniko, including multi-architecture images, image scanning, SBOMs and signing.

• 
Deployment pipelines: promotion from dev to staging to production with approvals and quality gates, plus blue-green, canary and fast rollback. GitOps with Argo CD or Flux, and database migrations as part of a release.

• 
Infrastructure pipelines: Terraform or Pulumi plan and apply from CI, with policy checks and drift detection.

• 
Pipeline security: short-lived credentials through OIDC federation or a secrets vault instead of long-lived keys, least-privilege deploy roles, and protected branches.

• 
Release engineering for our chain: building and publishing node binaries and images, and coordinating rolling upgrades across validator and RPC fleets.

• 
Delivery health: you track build time, build cost, flaky tests and DORA metrics (deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate, time to restore), and you cut wasted builds with ignore rules and caching.

Networking fundamentals

• 
TCP/IP, subnetting and CIDR, routing, NAT, and the difference between L4 and L7 load balancing.

• 
DNS, TLS and certificates, firewalls and security groups.

• 
Private connectivity: VPC design, peering, private endpoints, and keeping internal traffic off public IPs.

• 
Troubleshooting with dig, curl, mtr and tcpdump, and understanding what internet egress costs.

Also required

• 
Production experience on at least two of Google Cloud, AWS and Alibaba Cloud, and willingness to learn the third quickly.

• 
Terraform or Pulumi in production, plus scripting in Bash and in Python or Go.

• 
A track record of cutting a cloud bill with data, through rightsizing, cleanup or commitments.

• 
A security-first habit with production credentials, and clear written communication.

Nice to have

Running blockchain nodes in production, such as CometBFT validators and sentries, EVM archive or RPC nodes, and snapshot pipelines.

• 
Cloudflare Workers, Tunnels and Zero Trust at scale.

• 
Alibaba Cloud on the international site, including its billing and support model.

Confidential computing (Intel TDX) and GPU workloads.

CKA or CKS certification, a FinOps certification, or experience moving a team between CI systems, such as Jenkins to GitHub Actions.

Go or Rust, enough to read and patch the services you operate.

jobs.title: UI/UX Engineer
jobs.description:
Betriebliche Steuern sind kompliziert – Steuerberatung muss es nicht sein. Für die meisten Unternehmen bedeutet sie bis heute Papierstapel, lange E-Mail-Verläufe und Warten. Das wollen wir grundlegend ändern.

Bei b'steuern verbinden wir Steuerberatung, Software und KI von Anfang an miteinander. Unser Ziel ist nicht, eine klassische Steuerkanzlei einfach digitaler zu machen. Wir definieren neu, was Steuerberatung bdeutet: mit KI-Agenten, die ganze Arbeitsabläufe eigenständig übernehmen, und Software, die Menschen genau dort einbindet, wo sie gebraucht werden.

Daraus entstehen Designfragen, für die es noch kaum etablierte Antworten gibt: Wie übergibt man Arbeit an einen KI-Agenten? Wie behält man den Überblick, wenn mehrere Agenten gleichzeitig arbeiten? Wann kann man ihren Ergebnissen vertrauen? Und wie gestaltet man die Zusammenarbeit zwischen Menschen und KI so, dass sie sich einfach und selbstverständlich anfühlt?

Als UI/UX Engineer findest du Antworten auf diese Fragen – und setzt sie selbst in funktionierende Software um. Du gestaltest die Produkte, mit denen unsere Mandant:innen und unser Steuerteam täglich arbeiten. Und weil viele dieser Produkte und Prozesse noch gar nicht existieren, entscheidest du von Anfang an mit, wie sie aussehen sollen.

Deine Aufgaben

• 
Die Arbeit unseres Steuerteams neu denken. Du arbeitest direkt mit den Menschen zusammen, die unsere internen Werkzeuge täglich nutzen. Gemeinsam findet ihr heraus, wo Software und KI ihre Arbeit einfacher, schneller und besser machen können – und wie die passenden Werkzeuge dafür aussehen.

• 
Die Zusammenarbeit zwischen Menschen und KI gestalten. Unsere Agenten übernehmen zunehmend ganze Arbeitsabläufe. Du entwickelst die Interaktionen und Oberflächen, mit denen Menschen Aufgaben delegieren, Ergebnisse nachvollziehen, Entscheidungen treffen und bei Bedarf eingreifen können.

• 
Die Mandant:innen-Erfahrung weiterentwickeln. Du gestaltest, wie Mandant ihre Steuerangelegenheiten erleben: einfach, transparent und ohne unnötigen Aufwand. Sie sollen jederzeit wissen, was gerade passiert und was als Nächstes ansteht.

• 
Selbst gestalten und umsetzen. Du gehst von der ersten Idee über Prototypen bis zur fertigen Anwendung. Du entwickelst deine Lösungen selbst und bringst sie in den Livebetrieb.

• 
Unser Designsystem aufbauen und weiterentwickeln. Du schaffst die Grundlagen, mit denen wir auch bei schnellem Wachstum konsistente, intuitive und hochwertige Oberflächen entwickeln können.

Das bringst du mit

• 
Du kannst gestalten und bauen. Du hast Erfahrung darin, digitale Produkte zu konzipieren und selbst umzusetzen. Du denkst nicht in getrennten Design- und Entwicklungsphasen, sondern willst, dass aus guten Ideen funktionierende Software wird.

• 
Du verstehst Softwareentwicklung. Du hast bereits anspruchsvolle Softwareprojekte entwickelt und verstehst die technischen Zusammenhänge dahinter: von Anwendungslogik und Datenflüssen bis zu Schnittstellen und Architekturentscheidungen.

• 
Du hast ein gutes Gespür für UX. Du erkennst, wo Nutzer den Überblick verlieren, Informationen fehlen oder Interaktionen unnötig kompliziert werden. Klare Nutzerführung und durchdachte Details sind dir wichtig.

• 
Du denkst AI-native. Du hinterfragst ständig, wie du mit KI besser und schneller arbeiten kannst, experimentierst mit neuen Ansätzen und teilst erfolgreiche Workflows mit dem Team.

• 
Du übernimmst Verantwortung. Du brauchst keine fertig priorisierte Aufgabenliste. Du findest selbst heraus, was wichtig ist, triffst Entscheidungen auch bei unklaren Anforderungen und kannst sie begründen.

• 
Du diskutierst offen und konstruktiv. Du vertrittst deine Meinung, gibst klares Feedback und lässt dich vom besseren Argument überzeugen.

• 
Du sprichst sehr gut Deutsch und fließend Englisch und lebst in Berlin oder bist bereit, hierherzuziehen.

Erfahrung in einem anspruchsvollen Start-up, mit KI-Produkten und komplexen internen Werkzeugen ist ein Plus. Ein bestimmter Abschluss, ein klassischer Werdegang oder viele Jahre Berufserfahrung sind dagegen keine Voraussetzung. Entscheidend ist, was du bereits gebaut hast und wie du an Probleme herangehst.

Passt die Rolle zu dir?

Du fühlst dich bei uns wohl, wenn du …

• 
genauso gern exzellente Software baust, wie du über gutes Design nachdenkst,

• 
Lust hast, neue Interaktionskonzepte für die Zusammenarbeit zwischen Menschen und KI zu entwickeln,

• 
selbst herausfindest, welches Problem gerade am wichtigsten ist, statt auf eine fertige Aufgabenliste zu warten,

• 
Freude daran hast, Dinge aufzubauen, für die es noch keine etablierten Lösungen gibt,

• 
gern direkt mit Nutzern sprichst, Lösungen ausprobierst und aus Feedback lernst,

• 
offen über deine Arbeit diskutierst und dich vom besseren Argument überzeugen lässt.

Die Rolle passt eher nicht, wenn du …

• 
am liebsten ausschließlich Designs in Figma erstellst und die technische Umsetzung anderen überlässt,

• 
vor allem klar definierte Tickets und fertig priorisierte Aufgaben bearbeiten möchtest,

• 
feste Prozesse, enge Zuständigkeiten und ein großes Team mit spezialisierten Rollen erwartest,

• 
dich lieber auf die visuelle Gestaltung bestehender Produkte konzentrierst, statt auch grundlegende Produkt- und Interaktionsfragen zu lösen.

Warum b'steuern?

• 
Eine Branche neu gestalten: Wir bauen nicht einfach bessere Kanzleisoftware. Wir entwickeln eine neue Art der Steuerberatung, in der Software und autonome KI-Agenten einen großen Teil der Arbeit übernehmen.

• 
Software und Kanzlei unter einem Dach: Wir entwickeln unsere Produkte direkt im eigenen Kanzleibetrieb. Du kannst mit den Menschen sprechen, für die du baust, und neue Ideen unmittelbar im Arbeitsalltag testen.

Wachstum: Jeden Monat kommen viele neue Mandant dazu. Was du entwickelst, erreicht schnell immer mehr Menschen.

Flache Strukturen: Wir arbeiten selbstorganisiert. Es zählt das beste Argument, nicht der Titel oder die lauteste Stimme.

Kompetitives Gehalt: Wir bieten eine attraktive Vergütung abhängig von Erfahrung, Fähigkeiten und Impact.

Arbeitsort: Unser Büro am Hackeschen Markt mit lebendiger Teamkultur. Wir arbeiten 3–5 Tage pro Woche gemeinsam vor Ort.

Ein Anschreiben brauchst du nicht. Zeig uns lieber etwas, das du gestaltet und selbst gebaut hast und auf das du stolz bist.

Wir freuen uns auf dich!

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager (m/w/d)
jobs.description:
Ralph baut das Operating System für Wohnimmobilien. Der Markt ist riesig, und er läuft noch größtenteils auf Aktenordnern, Outlook und USB-Sticks. Wir sind der erste AI Property Manager, der auf einem eigenen Operating System läuft, und betreiben Gebäude damit End-to-End. Ralph OS automatisiert Zahlungen, Buchhaltung, Compliance und Kommunikation. AI-Agenten bereiten die Arbeit vor, und unser Team gibt sie frei. Die Hausverwaltung ist unser Einstieg. Das Ziel ist die neue Infrastruktur für die ganze Kategorie, mit Fintech, Versicherung und Finanzierung auf derselben Plattform. Heute verwalten wir über 10.000 Wohneinheiten und wachsen schnell, organisch und durch Zukäufe. Verantwortung bekommst du bei uns früh, und was du baust, nutzen wir direkt im Alltag.

Deine Rolle

Du verstehst, wie Hausverwaltung wirklich funktioniert, und machst daraus Produkte, die unseren Verwalter:innen und Eigentümer:innen die Arbeit spürbar leichter machen. Du setzt dich mit den Menschen zusammen, die täglich mit unseren Workflows arbeiten, findest das Problem hinter dem Problem und treibst die Lösung bis zum Rollout. Da AI die Art, wie Produkte entstehen, gerade schnell verändert, zählt bei uns vor allem, wie schnell du lernst und wie gründlich du Dinge durchdringst.

Deine Aufgaben

• 
Du verstehst unsere Verwaltungsprozesse im Detail, indem du mit Property Managern und dem Operations-Team arbeitest, und erkennst, wo Workflows an ihre Grenzen stoßen.

• 
Du führst neue Features ein und begleitest den Rollout, damit sie im Alltag wirklich genutzt werden.

• 
Du definierst die Metriken, die wir verfolgen müssen, und prüfst nach jedem Release, ob ein Problem im Rollout oder im Produkt liegt.

• 
Du planst und führst Experimente und Nutzertests durch, mit internen Nutzer:innen ebenso wie mit Eigentümer:innen.

• 
Du erkennst Engpässe, entwickelst Lösungsvorschläge und bringst sie in unsere Produkt-Roadmap ein.

• 
Enge Zusammenarbeit mit Tech, Geschäftsführung und unserem In-House-Verwalterteam und Input zur Verbesserung unserer Prozesse und Software

Das bringst du mit

• 
Berufserfahrung: Mind. 4 Jahre im Produktmanagement oder Erfahrungen in der Beratung

• 
Strukturierte, analytische Denkweise: Du gehst Probleme von Grund auf an und hörst nicht auf, bevor du die Ursache verstanden hast

• 
Neugier und Ehrgeiz, dich tief in komplexe Workflows einzuarbeiten, und Lust auf die direkte Arbeit mit deutschsprachigen Operations-Teams

• 
Hands-on-Mindset: Du packst an, baust gern Dinge und denkst unternehmerisch

• 
Du hörst gut zu, bist empathisch und holst im Gespräch die Informationen heraus, die du brauchst

• 
Flexibilität im Kopf: Du passt deine Arbeitsweise an, wenn AI Prozesse verändert

• 
Strukturierte Arbeitsweise, hohe Verbindlichkeit und Eigenverantwortung

• 
Starkes Kommunikationsvermögen & Offenheit für neue Herausforderungen und digitale Tools

• 
Deutsch: C1 oder höher & Englisch: C1 oder höher

Das bieten wir

• 
Modernes Setup: MacBook, iPhone und moderne Tools von Tag eins

• 
Eigenverantwortliches Arbeiten ohne Mikromanagement

• 
Hybrides Arbeiten

• 
Urban Sports Club Zuschuss

• 
Regelmäßige Team-Events, Team-Lunches und Getränke im Büro

• 
Eine Entwicklungsperspektive: Mit dem Wachstum von Ralph kannst du in eine Führungsrolle im Produktbereich hineinwachsen

Bewerbungsprozess

• 
Intro Call (ca. 30 Min.) mit Recruiting

• 
Kennenlerngespräch (ca. 30 Min., remote)

• 
Fachgespräch mit Tech inklusive erstem Teil der Fallstudie (remote)

Vor Ort in Berlin: zweiter Teil der Fallstudie und Kennenlernen von Kolleg:innen aus verschiedenen Teams

Optional: Finales Gespräch mit der Geschäftsführung

Angebot

Eckdaten

Standort: Berlin

• 
Arbeitsmodell: Hybrid

jobs.title: Manager: Compliance Advisory (and Data Protection)
jobs.location: London or remote within the UK
jobs.description:
About Griffin

Hi, we’re Griffin. We’re a fully regulated UK bank that powers the accounts and payments offerings of product-led fintechs and platforms like Uber, Yonder, Prosper, and Sidekick. By doing the heavy lifting behind the scenes, our customers can focus on what they do best - delivering amazing customer experiences.

We’ve grown rapidly since our launch in 2024, and today provide the banking backbone behind products in remittance, payroll, wealth, insurance, proptech, payments, neobanking and more.

We’re moving into card issuing, stablecoin infrastructure, and agentic finance next as we continue to support the next generation of product-led companies.

Learn more about what we do

Our culture

We believe that smart, motivated, conscientious people thrive in high-trust, high-autonomy environments and have done our best to create such an environment at Griffin. People who thrive here don’t require much hand-holding, and go out of their way to figure out how to contribute in the most valuable way possible.

We've been remote-first since we were established in 2017 and we remain so today. Work here is asynchronous and fully flexible - because we want to be a part of your life in a way that helps you to get the most out of both your work and home life.

We understand that our culture and ways of working aren’t for everyone, and we’re very intentional about our hiring process as a result. We won't hire people who don’t seem like a strong fit for our core values, even if they're otherwise extremely qualified.

Our strong culture has helped us to remain a mission-driven company as we have scaled, and gives our people a clear, explicit operating framework and the space to focus on delivering real value for our customers.

Learn more about our culture.

The Team

You'll join our Service guild and work across first line operations, sales and produt. Working closely with Protect (our second line) you'll be the first person dedicated to compliance within the team. You'll define what great compliance solutions look like. Then implement them , keeping Griffin's products and customer outcomes in shape as we grow.

The opportunity

We want compliance and data protection built into how we design, sell and run our products, not bolted at the end.

As our hands on compliance adviser in the first line (the teams who run the business and own its risks), you'll bring regulatory expertise to help our operations, commercial and product teams do exactly that. With card issuing and other launches coming up, there's plenty to get stuck into.

Compliance advisory is the heart of this role and will take around 70% of your time. You’ll also pick up a smaller, complementary slice of work as our Data Protection Officer (DPO), around 30% of your time. DPO experience is a plus but not essential, and we’ll train you if you need it.

What success looks like

In your first year, compliance advisory is where you’ve made your mark. You’ve sought out our operations, sales and product teams and shown them that working with you makes things smoother, not slower. Now they bring you in early by default. You’ve guided at least one major launch, like card issuing, from first idea to go live. You’ve put clear governance and outcome monitoring in place for our live products, so Protect (our second line risk and compliance team) sees fewer surprises and finds a stronger compliance foundation.

Alongside that, in the smaller DPO part of your role, you’ve taken ownership of our data protection agenda. You’ve gone looking for ways to improve, made the changes happen, and given our senior leaders an honest picture of where we stand.

To do this you'll be involved in:

Compliance advisory (around 70% of your time)

• 
Product development: turning regulation into clear requirements, customer journeys, T&Cs and fair value assessments, from first idea through product approval to launch, with data protection built in from the start.

• 
Product lifecycle management: keeping live products compliant through periodic fair value assessments, outcome monitoring, reviews, changes and closures.

• 
Sales: helping our commercial team check early whether potential partners fit our risk appetite, and reviewing sales material.

• 
Marketing: working on marketing materials, both ours and our customers’, to make sure they comply with regulation and our own policies, and that our financial promotions are properly challenged.

• 
Service (Operations): building regulatory and data protection requirements into how Service works day to day, with procedures and controls people actually use.

• 
Regulatory change: working out what new rules mean for us, and making sure the right teams make the right changes on time.

• 
Issues and reporting: investigating and fixing compliance issues, including personal data breaches, and reporting clearly on compliance risks and customer outcomes.

• 
Working with second line (Protect): bringing them in early, sharing the evidence they need, and acting on their challenge.

Data Protection Officer (around 30% of your time - training will be provided if needed)

Being our DPO means:

• 
advising our teams on their obligations, including data protection impact assessments (DPIAs) and transfer risk assessments (TRAs)

• 
monitoring how well we comply with the UK GDPR, other global data protection laws and our own policies

• 
training colleagues and raising awareness of data protection

• 
being our contact point for the ICO and for people with questions or requests about their data

As our DPO, you’ll report directly to our COO and have the independence you need to do the job well. We’ll involve you early in anything that affects personal data.

We expect you to shape this role: This description reflects what we need today. How you achieve these outcomes, where you focus your energy, how this role evolves—that's for you to define as you learn what our customers need and where our technical gaps are.

Your background

We need a proactive compliance doer first and foremost. You get stuck in without waiting to be asked, and you’re comfortable tackling regulations you haven’t met before. You use your experience and expertise to help our teams find simple, clear and compliant solutions. Your advice is balanced, easy to follow and focused on the risks that matter most. You want to push the business forward, and you see good compliance as part of how we get there.

To ensure this, we're looking for people who have:

• 
Compliance experience in the first (preferred) or second line of a UK regulated firm, ideally a bank, e-money institution or payments firm.

• 
Practical knowledge of the rules behind our products, like Consumer Duty, BCOBS, CASS, FISMA, the Payment Services Regulations and the Money Laundering Regulations. As well as familiarity with HMRC requirements like BBSI and AEOI reporting.

• 
Hands-on experience turning regulation into practical requirements for product, sales or operations teams.

• 
An openness to picking up data protection as part of the role: a genuine interest is enough, DPO experience isn’t required.

• 
A curious, questioning approach. You know the right questions to ask before signing something off, not just the rules to check it against.

• 
The confidence to challenge, clearly and kindly, when something isn’t right.

• 
A love of writing. We have a major amount of written documentation that you will be contributing to, and we place a high degree of importance on clarity and readability (you can find out more here about how we write).

Ideally, you would also:

• 
Have deep expertise in at least one specialist area, such as payments, cards, Consumer Duty, BCOBS, financial promotions or similar.

• 
Have been a DPO, or worked closely with one, in a regulated firm.

• 
Have worked in finance or banking.

What can we offer you?

We are an early stage startup and we're working hard to expand our benefits package. We're planning to add to this list in the future

jobs.description:
An Introduction to Primer

Primer is the unified infrastructure for global payments. We give finance and payments teams the visibility and control to reduce complexity, improve performance, and capture more revenue - all from a single platform.

Backed by Sofina, Peak XV Partners, ICONIQ, Tencent, Accel, and Balderton, we're building the payments layer the world's best companies rely on.

Watch our showcase >

Read up on our $100m Series C

Learn more about our culture >

Primer processes payments for some of the world's best companies, which makes us an attractive target and means getting detection and response right really matters. We're looking for a Security Engineer to join our Detection & Response function and own a meaningful slice of how we detect, investigate and respond to threats across our cloud infrastructure and SaaS estate.

You'll write and tune the detections in our SIEM, build the automation that speeds up how we react, and be a first responder when something looks wrong. You'll have real ownership of the areas you work on, and the freedom to shape how we detect and respond to threats across them.

You'll also work closely with our Application Security/Product Security engineers: what we learn from detections and incidents shapes how we build, and what they know about our products shapes what we look for.

What you'll be doing

Detection

• 
Build, tune and maintain detections in our SIEM (Elastic), and identify opportunities to onboard new log sources (e.g. AWS, Google Workspace, Kubernetes) and build new detections on top of them.

• 
Find what our current detections miss, and keep the rule set lean by removing what no longer adds value.

• 
Use Python and Terraform to build and maintain the infrastructure behind your detections and tooling.

Response

• 
Own investigation: triage, investigate, escalate and resolve security incidents, and write up findings clearly enough to stand on their own

• 
Lead routine incidents end to end, and take a clear role in larger ones, whether that's driving the investigation or keeping stakeholders informed

• 
Build runbooks and automations (Python, Tines or similar) to cut manual work out of triage and response

• 
Join our on-call rotation for incident response and monitoring

Across both

• 
Make and document risk decisions in your area, and know when to pull in others.

• 
Keep the controls you own audit-ready and contribute evidence for audits (e.g. SOC 2, PCI DSS).

• 
Use AI tools to work faster across detection and response, from drafting rules and queries to summarising investigations, while maintaining a healthy level of scepticism.

What we're looking for

• 
Real experience responding to security incidents, from first alert through to write-up

• 
Hands-on experience writing and tuning detections in a SIEM (Elastic, Splunk or similar), using frameworks like MITRE ATT&CK to reason about coverage

• 
Experience with cloud-native detection and response in AWS or Google Cloud

Experience with Terraform or other infrastructure-as-code

Experience with no-code security automation or SOAR-style tooling

• 
Exposure to compliance frameworks like PCI DSS, SOC 2 or ISO27001

• 
Background in fintech, payments or another regulated industry

• 
Experience using AI tools or agents in security work, and a clear view of where they help and where they don't

jobs.description:
ABOUT TIDE

At Tide, we help SMEs save time and money in the running of their businesses by not only offering business accounts and related banking services, but also a comprehensive set of highly usable and connected administrative solutions, from invoicing to accounting.

Tide is transforming the small business banking market and now supports over 2 million members globally across the UK, India, Germany and France.

Using advanced technology, all solutions are designed with SMEs in mind. With quick onboarding, low fees and innovative features, we thrive on making data driven decisions to serve our mission: to help SMEs save time and money so they can get back to doing what they love.

Tide facts:

  • Tide is available for UK, Indian, German and French SMEs
  • Over 2 million members globally and rapidly growing
  • Over $300 million raised in funding
  • 3,000 Tideans globally
  • Recognised with Great Place to Work certification three years in a row, and among India’s Top 50 Best Workplaces in Banking, Financial Services, and Insurance in 2026
  • We have offices in Central London, with a member support and technology centre in Sofia, Bulgaria, technology centres in Serbia, Romania, Lithuania and Hyderabad and offices in Gurugram, New Delhi, Berlin, Paris and Luxembourg

About You

We’re looking for a Senior Paid Social Manager who can strategically lead and scale our acquisition efforts across paid social channels in the UK and Europe. You’ll bring deep expertise in managing multi-million-pound budgets, a data-driven approach, and a proven track record of driving large-scale growth. You will be responsible for leading strategy, execution, and innovation in our paid social performance, ensuring we stay ahead of platform changes and industry trends. You’ll also have a clear view on how AI is changing performance marketing, and you’ll build a team that uses it well.

You’ll be a Meta expert, with hands-on experience across bidding strategies, audience segmentation, attribution, and creative testing. Additionally, you’ll have experience scaling campaigns across TikTok, Twitter, LinkedIn. You’ll be a martech-savvy professional, comfortable with tracking solutions, first-party data activation, working with MMPs and advanced attribution modeling.

You will play a key role in shaping Tide’s international expansion and long-term paid social strategy, ensuring that performance marketing continues to be a key growth driver. This is an opportunity to lead and grow Tide’s in-house Paid Social team as an AI-enabled team, making a significant impact on the business.

Some of the things you’ll be doing:

  • Owning and scaling paid social performance globally, ensuring we maximise efficiency and return on investment across all platforms.
  • Managing and optimising multi-million-pound budgets, using advanced bidding strategies and automation tools to drive sustained growth.
  • Building an AI-enabled paid social team, deciding which work AI should handle (creative production, reporting, bid and budget management) and which stays with people, then training the team to work that way.
  • Embedding AI into creative and testing workflows, using generative tools to develop concepts, copy and variants faster, with clear quality, brand and compliance checks.
  • Using AI and automation across the account, from platform tools such as Advantage+ to custom scripts, agents and reporting workflows that cut manual work.
  • Developing and executing the paid social roadmap, identifying new opportunities, testing innovative strategies, and expanding our presence across emerging platforms.
  • Driving a full-funnel approach, from awareness campaigns to high-intent lead generation and conversion, leveraging creative and audience insights.
  • Collaborating with cross-functional teams (Data, Product, Web, Creative, and more) to align paid social strategies with Tide’s wider growth objectives.
  • Championing attribution and measurement, ensuring best-in-class tracking, incrementality testing, and first-party data activation.
  • Leading creative strategy, working closely with designers and copywriters to continuously test and optimise assets for performance.
  • Staying ahead of industry changes, including privacy regulations (SKAD, ATT, IFDA), AI-driven platform updates, and new advertising solutions.
  • Building and mentoring a high-performing, AI-literate paid social team, shaping the function as we scale both in the UK and internationally.

You’ll be a great fit if:

  • You have 7+ years of experience in paid social marketing, managing large-scale campaigns across multiple platforms.
  • You have a proven track record of driving large volumes of B2B acquisition through paid social.
  • You’re an expert in Meta advertising (Facebook & Instagram), with deep knowledge of bidding strategies, audience segmentation, and ad creative best practices.
  • You have extensive hands-on experience with LinkedIn Ads, Twitter, TikTok, and other secondary paid social platforms.
  • You’re highly analytical, comfortable with incrementality testing, MMM, and data-driven decision-making.
  • You have strong technical knowledge of tracking solutions, attribution modeling, and martech tools (Appsflyer, GA4, GTM, CDPs, Looker/Tableau, etc.).
  • You have hands-on experience using AI in marketing, such as generative tools for creative and copy, LLMs for analysis, and automation for reporting and optimisation.
  • You have experience building or leading a team that uses AI day to day, including setting standards, sharing prompts and workflows, and measuring the productivity gain.
  • You’re comfortable with Meta’s AI-led campaign products (Advantage+, automated bidding) and know when to trust automation and when to override it.
  • You have sound judgement on AI risk, including brand safety, accuracy of claims and data privacy, ideally in a regulated industry such as financial services.
  • You understand how to drive performance across web traffic, mobile apps, and lead generation channels.
  • You have a test-and-learn mindset, with a structured approach to experimentation and optimisation.
  • You can effectively communicate complex insights, using data visualisation tools to tell compelling performance stories.
  • You have experience managing agency relationships, but also thrive in an in-house, hands-on environment.
  • You’re a natural leader, with experience mentoring and growing a team of paid social professionals.
  • Fluency in a second language (French or German) is preferable.

What you’ll get in return:

  • Make work, work for you! We embrace flexible working and remote-first arrangements.
  • 25 days holiday + bank holidays.
  • Vitality Health and Dental Insurance, with a proactive focus on mental and physical well-being.
  • £1,000 L&D budget per year, plus up to three L&D paid days off.
  • Enhanced family-friendly leave.
  • Work abroad for up to 90 days a year.
  • Snacks, drinks, and social events in our offices.

Tidean Ways of Working

At Tide, we’re Member First and Data Driven, but above all, we’re One Team. We trust our employees to work in a way that suits them while delivering great results. Our offices are always available for those who want

About the team 

The Business Management Software commercial team are responsible for driving adoption and usage of essential products for Small Business Owners. This includes Tide’s range of accounting packages, as well as invoicing, expense management, payroll and Company Formations / Company consistent value to members and a consistent revenue stream to Tide. The team works closely with Product, Finance, Business Insights, CRM and Operations teams to translate member and commercial insights into appealing product enhancements, effective positioning, and strategies that enhance engagement and retention. 

About the role 

We’re looking for an exceptional Lead Country Commercial Manager to scale revenue growth across our Accounting, Tax and Payroll products (part of our BMS suite, known internally as ‘Admin Services’) and build an indirect distribution channel via Partners & Accountants.

You will sit at the heart of Tide’s commercial function and be responsible for collaborating with cross-functional teams (mainly Marketing, Product, Finance) to understand funnel conversion, campaign(s) performance and product prioritisation, whilst owning competitor and market insight and leading new product go-to-market (GTM) launch plans. Excellent organisation, strategy and communication skills essential.

Key areas of this role:

  • Revenue Ownership & Forecasting: Partner closely with Finance and key stakeholders to set, track, and refine commercial projections for the Accounting, Tax & Payroll products ensuring revenue accountability and proactive identification of risks and opportunities.
  • Accountants Strategy & GTM planning: Research UK Accountants market and build a clear, concise and financially robust indirect model to help Tide scale their BMS products and others with Accountants.
  • Competitor and Market insight: Regularly analyse key competitor movements and wider industry trends - relevant to Accounting, Tax, Payroll and Accountants - translating insight into actionable strategies that strengthen and differentiate Tide’s positioning and value proposition.
  • Analytics-Driven Insight: Analyse (via BI team) member behaviour, segment audiences, subscription cohort performance and create clear recommendations to shape product prioritisation, pricing, positioning and communications.
  • Product Development: Partner with the Product teams to assess opportunities to shape product positioning, product led growth, aligning on roadmaps and supporting  successful product launches with tailored GTM strategies.
  • Launch Strategy: Support new feature launches across channels and operational teams to deliver best-in-class experiments. 
  • Stakeholder Management: High levels of communication with a wide range of stakeholders, including Tide’s Senior Leadership Team and Executives.
  • Member Obsession: You will be or become an expert in the core motivations of our members in order to focus on bringing their voice to commercial and product design discussions.

What we are looking for 

  • Strong commercial acumen:  Proven experience in driving commercial impact, partnering with finance to understand performance and identify opportunities to improve.  Able to set and track clear KPIs across all initiatives to meet revenue goals.
  • Accountancy software experience: Understanding of software and experience scaling software at either an Accountancy software company or with Accountants.
  • 5+ years’ experience leading ‘always on’ activity to drive commercial performance.   This will ideally be with specific experience in Accounting, Invoicing or Expense Management products, ideally in a fintech environment – key is demonstrated ability to plan and deliver consistent activity that drives commercial impact.
  • Strong analytical mindset: Able to review and interpret data to develop hypotheses and assumptions, turning insights into clear, actionable plans.
  • Proven GTM track record – delivering holistic, high impact omni-channel campaigns  (across sales, CRM, in-app contact points)
  • Exceptional project management skills, able to juggle multiple launches and tactical tests in a fast-moving environment.
  • Creative collaborator: Builds relationships across teams, crafts compelling messaging and navigates ambiguity with confidence.
  • Self-starter attitude: Works backwards from targets, removes blockers proactively and adapts when priorities shift.

What you’ll get in return

  • Competitive salary 
  • Vitality Health Insurance, with a proactive focus on mental and physical wellbeing
  • Hundreds of perks and discounts through Vitality Health Insurance (fitness watches, Waitrose cashback, gym membership etc.)
  • 24/7 Employee Assistance Programme
  • 25 days holiday with the ability to buy extra days
  • Professional L&D budget per year
  • Referral bonus when you bring your friends to join Tide 
  • Access to ‘salary sacrifice’ benefits such as Cycle to Work scheme and pension contribution
  • Spacious brand new office in Liverpool street with an all-day snacks bar
  • Enhanced family-friendly leave
  • 24 hours paid volunteering time off per year
  • Flexible work from home or at the office arrangements
  • Monthly team socials (we’ve had themed bingo, online cocktail making sessions, wellbeing challenges and themed virtual pub quizzes)
  • Sabbatical leave 

TIDE IS A PLACE FOR EVERYONE

At Tide, we believe that we can only succeed if we let our differences enrich our culture. Our Tideans come from a variety of backgrounds and experience levels. We consider everyone irrespective of their ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, family or parental status, national origin, veteran, neurodiversity or differently-abled status. We celebrate diversity in our workforce as a cornerstone of our success

Software Engineer - Research Participants - United Kingdom

 

 

Location: Remote (UK)
Type of contract: Freelance
Hourly Rate: £19 (pay based on actual study time)

About Prolific

Prolific is not just another player in the AI space – we are building the biggest pool of quality human data in the world.

Over 35,000 AI developers, researchers, and organizations use Prolific to gather data from paid study participants with a wide variety of experiences, knowledge, and skills.

The Role
Do you have a device with a microphone? Get paid to take part in voice interviews. We’re inviting software engineers and developers based in the UK to take part in a research study run by an institution focused on global policy change. This is a paid research participation opportunity, not a job as a software engineer. Quick signup, flexible schedule, real payouts. 

Your voice can help build a picture of how people across the UK think and talk about important issues, and that evidence is designed to inform real policy decisions. Every participant counts, and together we’re working toward a shared research goal.

The project launches in about one week, and places are allocated on a first come, first served basis, so please sign up as soon as you can.

What you’ll be doing

  • Taking part in a short voice conversation with another participant
  • Completing a short online survey sharing your views and experiences
  • Giving honest, considered responses based on your own perspective
  • Watching the community research goal progress as more participants take part

What you’ll bring

  • Residence in the UK
  • Fluent English
  • A device with a working microphone
  • No research experience or specialist research qualifications required. We want a genuine cross-section of the UK population.

Why join this project?
This is a chance to be part of something meaningful and have a say in research aimed at shaping policy. Once the findings are published, we’ll share them with participants so you can see the impact of your contribution.

Please note that you must be new to Prolific to sign up successfully. If you already have a Prolific account, there is no need to register again. Simply ensure your profile is up to date to be eligible for this and future opportunities.

Why Prolific is a great platform to join as a Participant

Joining our platform as a Prolific participant will give you the chance to influence the AI models of the future using your professional expertise. Once you pass our assessment, you can join Prolific in just 15 minutes, and start enjoying competitive pay rates, flexible hours, and the ability to work from home.

We've built a unique platform that connects researchers and companies with a global pool of participants, enabling the collection of high-quality, ethically sourced human behavioural data and feedback. This data is the cornerstone of developing more accurate, nuanced, and aligned AI systems.

We believe that the next leap in AI capabilities won't come solely from scaling existing models, but from integrating diverse human perspectives and behaviours into AI development. By providing this crucial human data infrastructure, Prolific is positioning itself at the forefront of the next wave of AI innovation – one that reflects the breadth and the best of humanity.

jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer, Event Streaming Systems
jobs.description:
Our Global Structure


Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we’re unlocking new possibilities as one global team.

Join us in our mission to transform the way people shop and eat, where impact, innovation and growth drive everything we do.

Our Engineering teams tackle complex technical challenges across a global, three-sided marketplace, building and scaling systems that serve millions of customers, riders and merchants every day. From real-time logistics to resilient infrastructure and marketplace optimisation, we design, build and operate technology that powers Deliveroo’s (& Doordash’s) growth at scale.

We’re looking for a Staff Software Engineer to join our Event Streaming Systems team. This is a hybrid role.

In this role, you’ll provide technical leadership for the event streaming infrastructure that powers business-critical workflows across Deliveroo, DoorDash and Wolt. You’ll help define the long-term direction of our messaging and streaming platforms, lead high-impact technical initiatives across teams, and raise the reliability, scalability and operational excellence bar for Tier-0 infrastructure.

What You’ll Be Doing

You’ll be joining the Event Streaming Systems team within the broader Storage organisation. The team builds and operates highly reliable, scalable and efficient event streaming infrastructure, including Kafka, Event Streaming abstractions (internally called EventBus), messaging platform capabilities, and future streaming technologies. The team also partners closely with Database Reliability, Storage, SRE, Data Platform and Core Infrastructure teams to ensure our most critical data and messaging systems remain reliable, operable and cost-efficient at global scale.

These systems support Tier-0 workflows and are foundational to how engineering teams build reliable, event-driven products at scale.

Here’s what your day-to-day might look like:

  • Define and drive the technical vision and roadmap for our event streaming and messaging platforms, balancing reliability, scalability, cost, operability and developer experience.
  • Lead team-level and cross-team initiatives for Kafka, EventBus and related streaming infrastructure, from ambiguous problem definition through architecture, delivery, rollout and adoption.
  • Act as a trusted technical advisor for Kafka, messaging, storage-adjacent and DBRE-related platform decisions across Deliveroo, DoorDash and Wolt.
  • Design durable, extensible systems and platform capabilities that can be leveraged by other engineers and teams, reducing duplicated effort and operational risk.
  • Lead the resolution of complex distributed systems problems, including reliability incidents, performance bottlenecks, capacity constraints, data-safety risks and production-operability gaps.
  • Raise the operational excellence bar for Tier-0 infrastructure through observability, automation, incident response, runbooks, operational readiness and continuous improvement.
  • Proactively build alignment with partner teams, including EventBus, Storage, DBRE, SRE, Data Platform and Core Infrastructure, shaping joint goals and mitigating cross-org delivery risks.
  • Mentor and grow engineers through technical guidance, design, feedback, code review, incident review facilitation and knowledge-sharing across the engineering community.
  • Evaluate emerging streaming, storage and automation technologies, including AI-enabled operational tooling where appropriate, and champion pragmatic adoption where they can materially improve quality, velocity or efficiency.

What You’ll Need to Thrive

Our ideal candidate will bring deep expertise in several of these areas and the judgment to lead others through ambiguity:

  • Significant experience building, operating and evolving distributed systems in production, ideally for platform or infrastructure teams supporting critical workloads.
  • Deep hands-on experience with Kafka or comparable event streaming systems as a platform, infrastructure service or business-critical production dependency.
  • Strong technical leadership skills, with a track record of defining technical direction, shaping roadmaps and leading multi-engineer or cross-team initiatives.
  • Ability to make and own technical decisions in ambiguous situations, using data, operational signals, customer needs and long-term system health to guide tradeoffs.
  • Strong coding ability in Java, Go, Python or similar languages, with a focus on reliable, maintainable, observable and scalable production systems.
  • Experience improving production reliability through automation, observability, capacity management, incident response, operational readiness and sustainable on-call practices.
  • Strong distributed systems fundamentals, including Linux, networking, storage, JVM-based systems, fault tolerance, backpressure, capacity planning and performance tuning.
  • A force-multiplier mindset: you create leverage through reusable technical foundations, clear documentation, strong engineering practices, mentoring and removing single points of failure.
  • Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence platform, infrastructure, product and reliability teams without relying on authority.

Nice to have

  • Experience contributing to Kafka or related open source distributed systems.
  • Experience with Redpanda, WarpStream, AutoMQ, Pulsar or similar streaming technologies.
  • Experience with JVM tuning, diskless streaming architectures or multi-region event streaming platforms.
  • Experience operating Tier-0 infrastructure at large scale, including incident leadership and post-incident improvement programs.
  • Experience with database reliability, storage systems, data platforms or DBRE practices in addition to event streaming.
  • Experience using automation or AI-assisted operational tooling to improve reliability, developer experience or incident response quality.

Why Join Us?

At Deliveroo (Doordash), you’ll do work that matters, solving real-world problems in a three-sided marketplace that’s constantly evolving.

We’re food lovers, problem solvers, community builders and more, brought together by a shared drive to make things better.

Working here you can expect to:

  • 🔧 Solve meaningful problems at real scale. Work on complex, always-on infrastructure that impacts millions every day.
  • 🌱 See your impact, fast. Shape the direction of foundational platforms used by teams across Deliveroo, DoorDash and Wolt.
  • 🧠 Grow through challenge and ownership. Lead ambiguous, high-impact technical problems with strong support from peers and leaders.
  • 🌎 A culture built for builders. High standards, collaboration, flexible working and continuous learning.
  • 💰 Share in the success you help create. Competitive salary and equity options, so you’re rewarded for the impact you make.

➡️ Want a deeper look at how we build? Check out our Tech Blog.

We aim to create a fair process that lets your skills shine. Our interview process typically includes 3–4 stages. Explore our Engineering Interview Guide to help you feel confident at each stage.

Our Global Structure

jobs.description:
Our Global Structure


Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we’re unlocking new possibilities as one global team.

Join us in our mission to transform the way people shop and eat, where impact, innovation and growth drive everything we do. Our People team are the architects of a great workplace where brilliant minds come together to do their best work. From discovering diverse talent and nurturing future leaders, to creating spaces that spark collaboration and crafting rewards that celebrate success—we’re passionate about building a culture where everyone can thrive.

We’re looking for a Senior HR Advisor to join our Manchester team. This is a hybrid role. You’ll help us deliver a fair, consistent and high-performing employee experience by leading complex employee relations, strengthening manager capability and using people insights to improve how we work across our Merchant organisation.

Get to know our People team—what drives us, how we work and what you can expect.

What You’ll Be Doing

You’ll be joining the UKI People team, primarily supporting our Merchant organisation. Employee relations sits at the heart of the role, alongside a broader focus on employee experience, operational excellence and continuous improvement.

Employee Relations and Case Management

  • Manage a varied and complex end-to-end caseload across performance, probation, absence, grievances and disciplinaries.
  • Provide clear, practical advice that balances employee experience, commercial needs, employment law and organisational risk.
  • Build trusted relationships with managers, helping them address concerns early and confidently challenging where needed to achieve fair and consistent outcomes.
  • Respond to sensitive employee and manager concerns with sound judgement, discretion and professionalism, ensuring issues are resolved or escalated appropriately.
  • Maintain accurate and timely case documentation, delivering a consistently high standard of support across competing priorities.

Employee Experience and Engagement

  • Partner with managers, leaders, and People colleagues to create an environment where employees feel heard, valued and supported.
  • Use employee feedback, case themes and engagement insights to identify emerging concerns and opportunities to improve the employee experience.
  • Support feedback channels and targeted engagement activity, ensuring themes are followed through and actions are clearly communicated.
  • Coach managers on the behaviours and everyday practices that influence engagement, performance and retention.

Root-Cause Analysis and Process Improvement

  • Use case data, employee feedback and people trends to identify hotspots and underlying factors, such as onboarding, management capability or gaps in existing processes.
  • Turn insights into practical interventions that reduce avoidable cases and improve employee and manager experiences.
  • Recommend continuous improvements to People policies, guidance and processes, helping us deliver support with greater consistency and efficiency.
  • Identify recurring employee or manager questions and improve the guidance, tools and self-service resources available to them.

Manager Capability and Coaching

  • Coach and upskill managers through sensitive people matters, helping them build the confidence and judgement to handle issues effectively.
  • Deliver practical sessions on employee relations policies, UK employment legislation and effective people management.
  • Guide managers towards the right People tools and resources, encouraging greater self-sufficiency while remaining available for complex or higher-risk situations.
  • Communicate complex processes and decisions clearly to a range of audiences, adapting your approach to the situation and the people involved.

People Partnering and Strategic Support

  • Partner with leaders across our Merchant organisation, building a strong understanding of their teams, priorities and people challenges.
  • Support core People processes, including performance calibrations, engagement activity and organisational change.
  • Use data and people insights to support leadership discussions and inform practical, evidence-based decisions.
  • Contribute to targeted UKI People projects and work collaboratively across the wider People team to deliver meaningful improvements.

What You’ll Need to Thrive

Essential

  • Significant experience managing complex end-to-end employee relations cases within a fast-paced environment, backed by up-to-date knowledge of UK employment law.
  • Strong advisory and coaching capability, with a proven ability to constructively challenge managers and balance commercial risk with employee experience.
  • Sound judgement and the confidence to navigate sensitive or ambiguous situations with limited direction.
  • An analytical mindset, with experience using case data, employee feedback and people trends to identify root causes and deliver proactive HR solutions.
  • Strong organisational skills and attention to detail, including the ability to maintain accurate documentation, meet deadlines and deliver consistently across multiple priorities.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex or sensitive information clearly to a range of audiences.
  • A high level of discretion and professionalism when handling confidential employee information.
  • A collaborative and adaptable approach, with experience building trusted partnerships across teams and influencing without direct authority.
  • Confidence using HR systems and digital tools to manage work, identify insights and improve the employee and manager experience.

Nice to Have

  • Experience supporting commercial, operational or technology-led business units.
  • Broader exposure to, or an interest in, HR Business Partnering and organisational design.
  • Experience supporting employee listening, engagement or retention initiatives.
  • Experience improving HR guidance, self-service tools or digital processes to increase adoption and make support easier to access.
  • Familiarity with people analytics or AI-enabled tools and an interest in how emerging technology can improve HR decision-making and operational efficiency.

Why Join Us?

At Deliveroo, you’ll do work that matters, solving real-world problems in a three-sided marketplace that’s constantly evolving.

We’re food lovers, problem solvers, community builders and more, brought together by a shared drive to make things better. Working here, you can expect to:

  • 🔧 Make a visible impact every day
    Your work directly improves experiences for customers, partners and riders.
  • 🌱 Learn fast in an entrepreneurial environment
    Work close to the market with autonomy, pace and real responsibility.
  • 🧠 Build a career, not just a role
    Stretch yourself, develop new skills and grow as the business evolves.
  • 🌎 Deliver together in an inclusive culture
    Join collaborative, values-driven teams that support you to do your best work.

jobs.title: Golang Backend Engineer, Financial Product Fraud
jobs.description:
Our Global Structure


Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we’re unlocking new possibilities as one global team.

Your job is to make sure every payout and transaction lands with the right person.

We have spent years getting very good at protecting the things a marketplace has always had to protect: checkout fraud, account takeover, courier abuse. But we are no longer only a marketplace. We now issue banking products, lend to merchants, move instant payouts to couriers, and collect cash on the doorstep. Every one of those is a new way for money to leave the platform.

This is a new team, and it owns that surface: fraud wherever money moves through the platform. Who receives it, who lends it, who collects it, and who holds it in a financial account. Think instant payout rails, merchant cash advances, and platform-issued banking and earned-wage products serving millions of couriers and merchants. These are live loss surfaces, and the volume grows with every financial product we launch.

We are now looking for a Backend Engineer (Golang) to build that protection. You will design and ship real-time detection and automated enforcement for our financial products across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo. The work is high-throughput, low-latency, and unusually consequential: a rule you ship on Monday can stop a serious loss by Friday. It is also close to greenfield, so you will be setting the patterns every future financial product inherits on day one.

This role will be based in London, UK as one of the founding engineering roles in our London hub, working closely with our teams in Helsinki and Berlin.

What you'll do:

  • Build and maintain high-throughput, low-latency backend services in Go that score financial events in real time, including payout enrollments, bank account links, credit applications, and account-to-account transfers.
  • Design fraud detection and automated enforcement for our financial products end to end: from signal collection through to the decision that blocks a fraudulent payout.
  • Build on and extend our shared fraud decisioning platform, so signals, rules, and models work across all three of our brands instead of being rebuilt three times.
  • Partner closely with risk analysts, data scientists, and product managers to turn observed fraud patterns into shipped detection, and to know when a rule, a model, or a product change is the right answer.
  • Work across team boundaries with our account security, payments fraud, and financial product teams. We build on their signals rather than rebuild them, so clean interfaces matter.
  • Contribute to architectural discussions and technical decisions as we establish the fraud infrastructure baseline for financial products, with support from senior engineers on the team.
  • Write well-tested, observable code and help the team hold a high quality bar. In fraud, a silent failure is a loss event.

Our expectations:

  • 3 to 6 years of professional software engineering experience, including backend services you have shipped and owned in production.
  • 1+ years of production experience in Golang, or strong experience in another backend language and real enthusiasm for picking Go up quickly.
  • A working understanding of low-latency, high-throughput distributed systems. Real-time decisioning comes with a latency budget, and you are keen to learn to build inside one.
  • Hands-on experience with SQL and/or NoSQL databases, and some exposure to event-driven architectures (Kafka or similar).
  • Willingness to operate what you build, including a share of on-call, with a pragmatic approach to reliability.
  • Uses AI tooling in day-to-day development and can critically evaluate its output for correctness and quality.

Nice to have

  • Experience in fraud, risk, payments, lending, or financial crime, especially money movement fraud, bank account linking fraud, payout abuse, or lending fraud.
  • Experience with rules engines, real-time feature stores, or ML model serving in a decisioning path.
  • Background in Kotlin, Java, Python, or Node.js alongside Go.
  • Familiarity with cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP).
  • Experience working across multiple brands, regions, or regulatory regimes.

What we value

  • A product-oriented mindset. You think beyond the ticket, understand the "why" behind the work, and take a high level of responsibility for outcomes rather than output.
  • Comfort with ambiguity. This is a new team on a new surface; parts of the charter are still being drawn, and you will help draw them.
  • A track record of owning a project or feature end to end, especially in fast-paced environments.
  • Clear and proactive communication, with a collaborative spirit. We work across three companies and several time zones, so we move fast, but we succeed together.
  • An adversarial instinct. The best fraud engineers enjoy thinking like the attacker.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

At Deliveroo, we know that a great workplace reflects the world around us and that true diversity and inclusion make us stronger, more creative, and better at what we do. We’re committed to fostering an environment where everyone can do their best work and feel they belong.

We believe in equality of opportunity and welcome candidates from all backgrounds regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, socio-economic background, religion, or belief.

If you have a disability or long-term health condition and need support to apply for one of our roles, or require any reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process, you’ll have the opportunity to let us know once you’ve submitted your application. We’ll share details on how to request support so we can ensure you have a fair and equitable experience.

If you’re excited about making a real impact in a fast-moving marketplace and growing your career alongside ambitious, supportive teams, we’d love to hear from you!


Beware of recruitment scams: DASH Brands will never ask you to pay money or share sensitive financial information during hiring — learn more about DASH Brands' legitimate recruiting process at careersatdoordash.com/recruitment-scam-awareness.

jobs.title: Senior Electrical Product Engineer - Maritime Engineering
jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

About the Role

The Senior Product Engineer is the primary electrical design engineering presence on the production floor, bridging the gap between design intent and production execution. The role sits within Platform Engineering and is based primarily at the production site, dispositioning nonconformances and Material Review Board (MRB) actions for electrical systems and sub-assemblies, resolving design questions in real time, and closing the loop between production and design so that issues get root caused and fixed at the source. To hold that authority credibly, this role also contributes to upstream electrical design - architecture, analysis, schematics, and design reviews - so they have the depth needed to make sound disposition decisions on the floor. This is a senior individual contributor role requiring strong technical judgement in electrical and power systems engineering, the ability to operate autonomously in a fast-paced production environment, and the credibility to influence both design engineers and production teams. You will be expected to drive systemic improvements, cutting repeat nonconformances through changes to the design and documentation, as well as resolving individual issues.

Key Responsibilities

Production Floor Engineering Support

  • Serve as the primary electrical design engineering point of contact on the production floor for assigned programs and product lines
  • Represent the design authority at Material Review Board (MRB) for electrical systems, working with Quality and Manufacturing to minimise production hold time without compromising product safety and integrity
  • Resolve production process-blockers, design ambiguities, and schematic/drawing interpretation issues in real time, exercising engineering judgement within defined authority boundaries
  • Provide rapid-response engineering support and Root Cause Analysis (RCA) to Production, Quality, and Test teams for electrical nonconformance resolution, use-as-is/rework/scrap decisions, and repair dispositions
  • Identify and escalate systemic electrical design issues to core Design Engineering teams with clear problem statements, data, and recommended corrective actions
  • Perform detailed electrical calculations, simulations, and analysis to support MRB dispositions, deviation requests, and use-as-is justifications (e.g. power budgets, thermal derating, circuit analysis, connector/harness assessments)

Electrical Design Contribution

  • Contribute to the design, development and integration of electrical systems and subsystems, maintaining the technical depth needed to hold disposition authority on the production floor
  • Perform detailed electrical calculations, simulations and analysis (circuit analysis, power budgets, thermal derating, EMC/EMI) to support both design decisions and MRB dispositions
  • Participate in design reviews (SRR, PDR, CDR) and contribute to system-level trade studies
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with mechanical, software, and systems engineering to integrate electrical systems into the vehicle

Design Intent Translation & Multi-Site Support

  • Support the translation of electrical design intent into production-executable work across multiple product versions, configurations, and manufacturing sites
  • Support the stand-up and ramp of production at new or expanding manufacturing sites, ensuring electrical design engineering knowledge transfers effectively
  • Raise and implement engineering changes to correct production issues that originate in the electrical design, through the Anduril configuration management and change process
  • Feed production observations, failure modes and DFM/DFA opportunities back into Platform Electrical design work through structured feedback, prioritised using data

Design to Production Interface

  • Collaborate with Manufacturing Engineering on work instruction (WI) development, tooling validation, and First Article Inspection (FAI) activities for electrical assemblies, communicating the design intent and acceptance criteria
  • Own the resolution of EBOM discrepancies found in production for electrical assemblies, and give engineering input to Configuration Management and Manufacturing Engineering on PLM workflows, BOM reconciliation and work instruction tooling
  • Identify patterns across electrical nonconformances, test failures and build issues, and lead engineering root cause analysis and design corrective action implementation
  • Collaborate on the improvement of key tool and functional interfaces (PLM workflows, digital work instructions, BOM reconciliation) that impact design-to-production efficiency
  • Support the development of scalable frameworks for multi-site production: configuration management alignment, site-specific work instruction adaptation, and cross-site lesson-learned sharing
  • Build repeatable playbooks for standing up production of new product variants, reducing ramp time and first-unit defects at each additional site

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Metrics

  • Maintain strong working relationships with Quality, Supply Chain, Manufacturing Engineering, and Program Management to ensure aligned priorities and rapid issue resolution
  • Collate and drive corrective actions on design-originated production issues, providing data-backed prioritisation to core Design Engineering teams
  • Participate in Production readiness reviews, design reviews (P&DFMEA, DFM/A/T) and engineering change assessments

Key Competencies & Attributes

  • Engineering Judgement: Technical depth in electrical and power systems combined with production pragmatism - able to make sound engineering decisions under time pressure without over-engineering solutions
  • Design Authority Integrity: You protect product safety and integrity under schedule pressure, understand the limits of your delegated authority and escalate when you should
  • Cross-Functional Influence: Credibility with both design engineers and production operators; able to speak both languages and bridge communication gaps
  • Autonomy & Initiative: Comfort with ambiguity and competing priorities in a fast-moving production environment; able to self-direct and prioritise without constant direction
  • Systems Thinking: Thinks beyond individual issue resolution to identify patterns, root causes, and scalable solutions that prevent recurrence across sites and variants
  • Communication: Clear, concise technical communication - written dispositions, engineering reports, and presentations to leadership

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering or a related field
  • Proven experience in a senior role within defence, tech or any fast-paced environment, driving successful electrical engineering projects from concept to mark

jobs.title: Manufacturing Test Engineer
jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology.
