jobs.title: Hyperscaler & Systems Integrator Partner Manager (North America)
jobs.description:
About ElevenLabs

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

• 
ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

• 
ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

• 
ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.

How we work

• 
High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

• 
Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

• 
AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

• 
Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

• 
Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.

What we offer

• 
Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

• 
Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

• 
Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

• 
Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

• 
Annual company offsite: Each year, we bring the entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia and Italy.

• 
Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

About the role

We’re looking for an experienced partnerships leader to own and scale ElevenLabs’ strategic relationships with cloud hyperscalers and Systems Integrators, the companies whose platforms, field teams and delivery capacity sit at the heart of how enterprises buy and deploy voice and customer experience AI.

You’ll build and manage co-sell and marketplace programmes with AWS, Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud, and build joint GTM and delivery motions with Regional and Global Systems Integrators. The goal: get ElevenLabs deeply embedded in hyperscaler partner networks and SI practices, so that when enterprises modernize their contact centers or build on cloud infrastructure, ElevenLabs is the natural AI voice layer, and partners have both the incentive and the capacity to sell and deliver it.

This is a 0→1 build in a high-leverage category. You’ll design co-sell and SI GTM frameworks, drive pipeline with hyperscaler field teams, structure marketplace and private offer motions, negotiate referral, resell and joint-offering agreements with SIs, and own the revenue and pipeline outcomes that come from these relationships.

jobs.title: Staff Engineer - Platform & Tooling
jobs.description:
Who is Atominvest

Atominvest is the operating system for modern private markets asset managers. Our modular, flexible SaaS technology underpins key investor- and portfolio-management workflows.

Our customers are sophisticated private equity, growth equity, and private credit firms managing billions in assets globally. We aim to deliver ongoing high-quality outcomes for them through a long-term partnership mindset.

At Atominvest, you’ll be working on something very exciting: the future of work, investments and sustainability/ ethical investing for the world’s best investors and delivering a positive impact through this. Based on the growth we are experiencing, we think we’re on to something big.

It won’t be easy. Joining a scale up business is an amazing and rewarding challenge, pushing well beyond the boundaries of natural growth cycles. You’ll move quicker than feels comfortable and be brilliant at continually re-prioritizing what must get done to keep Atominvest growing year over year at the pace of the best SaaS companies on the planet.

We’ve gone from zero to ten, now we’re looking to go from ten to one hundred!

About the role

Hi, I'm Thomas, VP Engineering at Atominvest. This is the hire I'm most excited about, so I wanted to tell you about it myself.

You'll own the platform our clients run on and build the AI development harness our engineers work in day to day. That work runs from infrastructure to application code, so we're looking for an experienced engineer with breadth across both, and depth in at least one. Together, it's what lets a small, lean team, working alongside AI agents, ship like a much bigger one.

By platform, we mean everything our product and our engineers stand on: infrastructure, security, test automation, developer experience, and the agent pipelines that run through all of them. It's a broad, hands-on role. You'll write infrastructure as code for a new service one day and address network vulnerabilities the next, then enhance our AI development harness and release a new feature, all within the same month.

You might be a platform engineer who loves shipping product, or a full-stack engineer who has run serious production infrastructure. Either works.

As deployments grow more complex, the team needs your depth in infrastructure and distributed systems. You'll strengthen the architecture and make the design decisions the platform will rest on for years. Those decisions should leave room to grow, because future products may bring much larger volumes of data than we handle today.

It has to stay dependable while we do it. Our software needs to be available around the clock, every day of the year, and data integrity is critical. Our clients use Atominvest to report to their own investors, so a wrong number matters as much as an outage. Security, reliability and audit-readiness matter too. If you enjoy getting those right without slowing everything else down, you'll find plenty of fun things to work on.

The machine that builds the product

We're becoming AI-native. Agents do more and more of the mechanical work of writing code, and engineers build the machine that builds the product: the architecture, the specs, the limits agents work within, and the evals that tell us whether their output is right.

I think that moves an engineer's leverage upstream. When code is cheap, the scarce things are judgement and understanding. Which problem is worth solving? What does good look like for the person using it? Is the output actually right? Did what we shipped help? The best engineers I've worked with always solved the end problem, with code as the medium. Now that's most of the job.

That's why product and user understanding sit at the centre of how we work. An engineer who knows our clients' workflows can point agents at the right problem and spot when the result is subtly wrong. Without that, agents just build the wrong thing faster.

Your part is the AI development harness that makes this safe. That means sandboxed environments with synthetic data, scoped and audited access to logs and alerts, and evals and validation gates in CI. It also means firm lines, enforced by tooling, that keep production deploys and secrets in human hands, and client data out of reach of development agents.

You'll also build the agent orchestration pipelines that run in three places: in how we build software, in AI workflows inside the product our clients use, and in the internal tools our implementation team uses to onboard and configure clients.

What you'll do

Build the machine that builds the product

Most of your time goes here.

• 
Build our AI development harness. Self-service infrastructure, a reproducible development environment, and the sandboxes, guardrails and evals that let agents take on more of the work safely, with results we can measure.

• 
Automate quality. Build the QA automation pipeline: automated tests, validation gates and release checks that give us confidence in every change, including the ones agents write.

• 
Orchestrate agents across the business. Build pipelines that run agents reliably and safely in our product workflows and our internal implementation tools, not just in engineering.

Own the platform

• 
Own our infrastructure. We're migrating to ECS. You'll strengthen our ECS architecture, see the move through in safe, reversible stages, bring every resource under infrastructure as code, and retire the old deployment model.

• 
Build security into the platform. Tenant-scoped credentials, per-tenant secrets, least-privilege access, and the audit trail that SOC 2 and our clients' security teams expect.

• 
Make production observable. Set up the monitoring, alerting and tracing we rely on, and build playbooks for on-call and incident response which is shared amongst the team.

Work across the stack

• 
Make the application changes the harness needs, such as synthetic data, test hooks and the specs agents work from.

• 
Ship product. Pick up application work in TypeScript and React alongside the team. Over time, you'll learn the codebase as well as the platform it runs on.

• 
Grow the team around you. Write the design notes and runbooks, pair with and review the work of other engineers, and mentor those who want to grow into infrastructure, so the platform never depends on one person.

Your first six months

• 
Get the first parts of "the machine" running, and show that they make the team faster without lowering quality.

• 
At the moment all of our end to end testing is done manually by our Product team. That's a massive manual overhead that bottlenecks our product development. You'll help build our AI-powered QA automation pipeline, so every change, whether a person or an agent wrote it, is tested automatically before it reaches clients.

• 
Strengthen the ECS architecture and complete the move with no disruption to clients.

• 
Get the platform fully into code, with tenant isolation and least privilege designed in.

• 
Put in place the monitoring and on-call foundations the team will build on.

How you'll work

You'll own this area rather than work through a ticket queue. You'll decide what to build and when it's good enough, write your decisions down so others can challenge them, and tell us when something isn't worth doing. You'll work closely with Product from the start of significant work, because the platform exists to serve clients and the engineers building for them.

You and I will work together every day. We'll shape the technical direction together and think through the hard calls, and you'll have a direct line to every decision that affects your work. I'll back your judgement, and I'll expect you to push back when you think I'm wrong.

This is an individual contributor role, but we expect you to multiply the team: leading different areas at different times, and delivering through others as well as through your own work.

jobs.description:
Product Engineer | Design Engineering Knowledge

Location: Cambridge (UK), hybrid with up to 2 remote days per week

Team: Product

Start date: ASAP

About Neural Concept

Neural Concept is the engineering intelligence platform used by leading manufacturers in automotive, aerospace, and energy. We combine geometric and physics AI with LLM-based agents so engineering teams can move from customer requirements to validated designs in a fraction of the usual time.

About the role

Design decisions depend on information that lives outside the CAD model: customer requirements, design rules, manufacturing and assembly constraints, and cost targets. This information is spread across specification documents, handbooks, ERP systems, requirements management tools, and system models. Engineers gather it by hand, often late in the process, and conflicts surface at design reviews or on the production line.

We call the capability that closes this gap Design Engineering Knowledge. It connects the design to the information ecosystem around it, so requirements, constraints, and trade-offs are available to engineers and AI agents while they work on the design itself.

As a Product Engineer, you will build this capability. Requirements are the first focus area: extracting them from customer specifications and requirements management systems, structuring them, and keeping them traceable. You will then extend the same foundation to design rule checks, Design for Manufacturing (DfM), Design for Assembly (DfA), and Design for Cost, and connect it to the enterprise systems where this knowledge already lives.

You will work with the Product Manager, solution engineers, and customer engineering teams, as the primary developer from the first customer conversation to the version running in production.

What you will do

• 
Build the requirements foundation: ingest customer specifications and RFQ packages, extract requirements with LLM and agent-based pipelines, and keep each one traceable to its source document and page.

• 
Extend this foundation to design rules, DfM, DfA, and Design for Cost, turning standards, handbooks, and company know-how into constraints that software and agents can use.

• 
Bring requirements, constraints, and trade-offs into the design workflow, so engineers can check a design against them at any stage and see which ones apply to the part they are working on.

• 
Build integrations with the systems around the design: requirements management systems, ERP (cost, materials, and supplier data), and system design and MBSE tools for architecture and system-level requirements.

• 
Design the data model that links requirements, rules, and constraints to parts, design parameters, and simulation results.

• 
Create evaluation sets and quality metrics with customers, so extraction and checking accuracy is measured and improves with every release.

• 
Design human-in-the-loop review flows where engineers validate and edit AI output, with versioning and a full audit trail.

• 
Spot recurring patterns across customers and turn them into reusable components of the Neural Concept platform.

Who you are

Must have

• 
Experience building and shipping production Python software in fast-moving, cross-functional teams.

• 
Hands-on experience with LLM applications in production: structured outputs, retrieval-augmented generation, agents, and evaluation.

• 
Experience integrating with enterprise systems through APIs and data models, for example ERP, PLM, or requirements management tools.

• 
Experience with document processing, such as PDF parsing, OCR, or information extraction.

• 
Strong software practices: testing (pytest), CI, packaging, code review, and git.

• 
A product mindset. You talk to users, understand the problem before writing code, and ship in small, measurable steps.

• 
Clear, concise communication with both customer engineers and internal teams.

• 
Based in Cambridge (UK) or willing to relocate.

Nice to have

• 
Background in mechanical engineering or physics, with exposure to DfM, DfA, or design-to-cost practices.

• 
Familiarity with requirements engineering and model-based systems engineering (MBSE, SysML).

• 
Experience working with CAD data or geometry processing.

• 
Experience with vision-language models, vector databases, or search ranking.

What you get

• 
Ownership of a product capability that customers use in real engineering programs, with direct access to the engineers who use it.

• 
A competitive salary and rewarding opportunities as we continue to scale.

• 
A collaborative, multicultural team where your work is visible and recognized.

• 
Colleagues who share knowledge freely and support each other.

• 
A hybrid model and flexible hours. We focus on results and trust you to organize your time.

We're proud to be an equal opportunity employer, and we're committed to building a diverse and inclusive environment where you can thrive.

About us 

Riverlane’s mission is to master quantum error correction (QEC) and unlock a new age of human progress. From advances in material and climate science, to complex chemistry simulation for new drug design, quantum computers will help humanity solve some of its most important challenges. But without QEC, the industry’s defining technical challenge, such breakthroughs can never be achieved.  Riverlane is the world leader in QEC technology. QEC is a complex problem that requires a range of skills, talent and passion.  

Having raised more than $125M in funding to date to accelerate our cutting-edge R&D in quantum error correction (QEC), Riverlane partners with many of the world’s leading quantum hardware providers and government agencies to make fault-tolerant quantum computing a reality. We’re making remarkable progress and growing fast.  

 

About the role

We have an exceptional opportunity for a Verification / Senior Verification Engineer to join our talented team of hardware designers and embedded software engineers. Together, you’ll deliver fully verified, high-performance, and trusted systems.   

In this exciting role you'll have end-to-end visibility across the entire stack, owning every aspect of verification and shaping how quality and reliability are built into our cutting-edge technology. You do not need a background in quantum computing! You will learn this along the way. 

 

What you will do  

As a Verification / Senior Verification Engineer at Riverlane, you will: 

  • Proactively work with designers and architects to define verification plans based on design specifications. You will take full ownership of detailed test strategies across block-level and system-level designs.  
  • Develop and implement scalable testbenches, including checkers, reference models and coverage groups in SystemVerilog. You will implement self-testing, directed and random tests to ensure every part of the system performs flawlessly.  
  • Maintain the health and evolution of the design verification environment, tracking of regressions, coverage metrics and bugs to ensure our systems meet the highest standards of quality and reliability. 

 

What we need  

  • Demonstrable commercial experience in functional verification, including ownership of verification planning and strategy.  
  • Proven experience of testbench design with verification frameworks like UVM/OVM.  
  • Knowledge of SystemVerilog assertion (SVA).  
  • Exposure to different programming languages, such as C, C++ and Python.  
  • A proactive person who can independently define the scope of work. 
  • A collaborative person with excellent communication skills, who actively shares (and listens to) constructive feedback. 
  • Ability to work effectively with ambiguity and changing requirements. 
  • Experience debugging across RTL, simulation, and hardware 

 

Even better if… 

  • Formal verification experience. 

 

What can you expect from us 

  • A comprehensive benefits package that includes an annual bonus plan, private medical insurance, life insurance, and a contributory pension scheme  
  • Equity, so that our team can share in the long-term success of Riverlane  
  • 28 days annual leave, plus bank holidays and enhanced family leave  
  • A diverse work environment that brings together experts in many fields (including software and hardware development, quantum information theory, physics and maths) and over 20 different nationalities

QEC is a complex problem that requires a range of skills, talent and passion.  

Having raised more than $125M in funding to date to accelerate our cutting-edge R&D in quantum error correction (QEC), Riverlane partners with many of the world’s leading quantum hardware providers and government agencies to make fault-tolerant quantum computing a reality. We’re making remarkable progress and growing fast.

jobs.title: Senior Backend Engineer
jobs.description:
About Payflows

At Payflows, we build software that helps large companies manage and automate their payment workflows. It’s not the flashiest part of a business, but it’s one of the most critical: invoices, approvals, payments, and controls. When these things slow down, the whole company feels it.

But our ambition goes further than just building a better workflow tool.

We believe the future of finance operations is not faster clicking: it’s no clicking at all 🫳 🎤

Finance teams shouldn’t spend their days moving data from one screen to another. Software should do the operational work, and humans should focus on reviewing, approving, and making the decisions that matter.

That’s the direction we’re building toward: an agent-driven finance platform, where intelligent agents handle the repetitive tasks, and users stay in control.

We started in 2022 with a small team and a rough first version of the product. Three years later, we’re working with major companies across France, the UK, and the US while choosing to keep our team small and human-sized.

We moved fast, shipped a lot, and not everything was built in a perfect way. But it helped us learn quickly, sign real customers, and prove that the problem we’re solving truly matters.

In 2024, investors trusted us with a $25M Series A. That gives us the chance to keep growing while also strengthening our foundations and building the system that will power this agent-driven future.

Today, we’re about 35 people from many different countries, and we’re looking for a few amazing humans to join the next chapter. 🤗

🚀 What you’ll actually do

You’ll help build a product that real finance teams rely on every day.

For us, engineering is not just about clean code, it’s about reliability, clarity, and trust, especially when money and automation are involved.

In a typical week, you might:

• 
Design and implement new services for a product feature.

• 
Refactor an early service to make it more robust.

• 
Investigate a performance or production issue.

• 
Work with product and frontend to shape a new feature.

• 
Review code and help teammates improve.

• 
Build backend tools that our AI agents use to perform real finance operations.

• 
Design safe, deterministic workflows where agents propose actions and humans review them.

Your time will be split between building new features and improving what already exists. Both matter.

You won’t just build endpoints. You’ll help shape the execution layer that our agents rely on: the APIs, data models, and workflows that let them act safely in production.

You’ll work closely with product, frontend, and customer-facing teams. We expect engineers to take ownership of parts of the system and help make them more reliable over time.

💻 Our current tech reality

Our stack evolves based on our challenges, but we care more about good design than trendy tools 🙏

Python is our core language. It helps us move fast, keep the code readable, and fits naturally with our AI-driven approach. A growing part of the system is built around agents that use our backend as a set of reliable, deterministic tools.

• 
Core language: Python

• 
Backend: FastAPI + Pydantic

• 
Data: PostgreSQL

• 
Infra: AWS, serverless when it makes sense

• 
Performance: some Rust for critical paths

• 
Architecture: multi-service backend, simple enough to reason about

Some parts of the system are clean and well-tested. Others were built quickly and need love. That’s the phase we’re in.

Over the next year, we’ll focus on:

• 
Turning core workflows into reliable tools for our agents

• 
Simplifying services

• 
Improving tests and observability

• 
Making performance more predictable

• 
Cleaning up early code

We know we’re not perfect, but we care a lot about improving step by step.

✨ Who’s going to thrive with us

You’ll probably feel comfortable here if:

• 
You like building products people actually use.

• 
You are autonomous and take ownership of what you ship.

• 
You take initiative and lead by example.

• 
You’re curious and enjoy figuring things out.

• 
You’re pragmatic about trade-offs.

• 
You communicate with kindness and clarity.

This role is a great fit if you’re excited by the idea of:

• 
Building systems that are used by AI agents, not just humans.

• 
Designing reliable, safe automation in production.

• 
Working on a product that is still early and evolving quickly.

You don’t need to know everything about AI. But you should be curious about it and excited to work in a system where agents are part of the core product 🤖

🧩 What you’ll get from this role

• 
Real ownership over parts of the system.

• 
Direct impact on customers and product decisions.

• 
A small, human team where your work is visible and meaningful 🤝

• 
A mix of feature work, system design, and technical improvements.

• 
Exposure to real scaling and production challenges.

• 
The chance to help build an agent-driven product from the inside.

We offer:

• 
Competitive salary and equity.

• 
Flexible remote setup (we prefer people to come into Paris or London office twice per week. At a minimum we’d ask you to be at an office 3 days per month, onboard in Paris for your first few weeks, and work CEST timezone).

• 
A high-autonomy environment where you have real ownership and space to make an impact.

• 
Plenty of room to grow, take responsibility, and shape parts of the product.

• 
A culture based on trust, ownership, and clear communication.

This isn’t a huge corporate environment. In exchange, you get autonomy, responsibility, and the chance to shape a product that’s still early in its story—and help build what finance operations will look like in the next decade 🚀

jobs.title: DevOps / Infra Lead
jobs.description:
🌍 Our Vision & Mission

At Payflows, we give finance teams the tools to reclaim their time and energy. Our platform weaves together banking connectivity, payments, AI, and procurement so they can ditch the busywork and focus on what really moves the needle.

🤝 Why Join Us?

We’re a small, mighty team who’ve earned our stripes at Airbnb, Luko, BNP Paribas, and Facebook. It’s not always easy—things move fast, and we expect a lot—but if you’re hungry for impact, you’ll find it here.

🛠️ We’re builders at heart. We move fast, think deeply, ship often — and we’re always hungry to learn more. You'll collaborate closely with product and tech to craft elegant backend systems that scale as fast as we do.

🚀 What You’ll Do

You'll own the infrastructure for a product that real finance teams rely on every day.

For us, infrastructure is not just about uptime; it's about reliability, security, and trust - especially when money and automation are involved. The platform has to be boring in the best possible way: predictable, observable, and safe to deploy to.

• 
In a typical week, you might:

• 
Evolve our infrastructure-as-code to add a service, a queue, or a whole new environment.

• 
Improve our CI/CD pipelines so engineers ship safely and fast, dozens of times a day.

• 
Investigate a production issue: a latency spike, a failing deploy, a database under load.

• 
Strengthen observability with dashboards, alerts, and traces, so we catch problems before customers do.

• 
Harden our security, secrets management, and access controls.

• 
Tune cost and performance across our AWS footprint.

Your time will be split between building new platform capabilities and making what already exists more reliable. Both matter.

You'll help shape the foundation that everything else stands on: the pipelines, environments, and guardrails that let engineers and our AI agents act safely in production.

You'll work closely with backend, frontend, and the AI team. We expect you to take ownership of the platform and make it more reliable over time, not wait for tickets.

💻 Our current tech reality

Our stack evolves based on our challenges, but we care more about good design than trendy tools 

We're an AWS shop, and we lean on managed services and infrastructure-as-code so the system is reproducible and easy to reason with. A growing part of our world is making the backend a set of reliable, deterministic tools that AI agents can call, which raises the bar on reliability even further.

• 
Cloud: AWS

• 
Infra-as-code: Pulumi (Python)

• 
Compute: ECS + Lambda, serverless when it makes sense

• 
Data: PostgreSQL on RDS/Aurora

• 
CI/CD: GitLab CI

• 
Orchestration: Airflow (MWAA)

• 
Observability: Grafana Cloud, CloudWatch, Sentry

• 
Auth & identity: Cognito, IAM

Edge & frontend: API Gateway, ALB, AWS Amplify for the web app

Some of this is clean, version-controlled, and reproducible. Other parts grew fast and live a little too much in people’s heads instead of in code. Closing that gap is a big part of why this role exists.

Over the next year, we'll focus on:

• 
Making every environment reproducible from code

• 
Better observability and alerting, fewer surprises

• 
Tightening the security and compliance posture that comes with handling enterprise finance data

• 
Faster, safer deploys

• 
Keeping AWS costs sane as we scale

🧑‍💻 What we’re looking for

• 
5+ years of experience with Python or any other OOP language

• 
Backend expertise: APIs, microservices, architecture best practices

• 
Databases & SQL: Data modeling, query optimization

• 
Git lover: Comfortable with version control and code reviews

• 
Pragmatic engineering mindset: Build, test, refine, simplify—smart shortcuts when time is tight

🧩 Bonus points if you’ve worked on:

• 
B2B SaaS or finance/ERP tools

• 
BaaS APIs or payment infra

• 
Serverless, AWS, event-driven architecture exposure

✨ Who's going to thrive with us

You'll probably feel comfortable here if:

• 
You think in systems and instinctively automate yourself out of repetitive work.

• 
You treat infrastructure as code, not as pets.

• 
You stay calm during incidents and are genuinely good at root-causing.

• 
You care about security, because you're handling other people's money.

• 
You are autonomous and take ownership of what you ship.

• 
You take initiative and lead by example.

• 
You're pragmatic about trade-offs.

• 
You communicate with kindness and clarity.

You don't need to know everything about AI - but you must be curious about it and excited to build the reliable foundation that agents run on 🤖

🧩 What you'll get from this role

• 
Real ownership over the platform the whole company runs on.

• 
Direct impact on reliability, security, and how fast every engineer can ship.

• 
A mix of platform building, system design, and reliability work.

• 
Exposure to real scaling and production challenges.

• 
The chance to help build the foundation of an agent-driven product from the inside.

jobs.description:
Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

As the Enterprise Customer Success Leader, you are tasked with more than just facilitating the adoption of our technology. As a member of the broader Customer Success Leadership team, you will craft and execute a strategic vision for ensuring customers reach their desired outcomes, emphasizing scalability, process rigor, and the development of playbooks to fuel expansion and mitigate churn.

Through empathetic leadership and a focus on value, you will spearhead efforts to enhance renewal and expansion rates, manage and develop talent, and drive forward customer relationships with proactive engagement.

You will also play an integral part in helping to drive strategy and execution in how we deliver an end-to-end excellent customer experience.

What You'll Do

• 
Lead by Example: Lead a dynamic customer success team towards exceptional performance, promoting a culture of accountability, execution, growth, and relentless improvement.

• 
Scalability and Process: Develop and implement strategic improvements to drive scalable strategies and playbooks, ensuring a systematic approach to all stages of the customer journey, including: implementation, adoption, value realization, retention, and expansion.

• 
Talent Coaching and Development: Inspire and mentor your team, elevating their capabilities to become strategic partners through influencing and advising decision makers and fostering customer advocacy.

• 
Advance Customer Relationships: Deepen client engagements through strategic interactions, serving as an advisor and advocate for key stakeholders, driving advocacy, organic growth, and referrals.

• 
Own Retention: introduce processes and early warning systems to reduce churn, mitigate risk, and ensure we are multi-threaded within customer accounts.

• 
Effective Collaboration: Work with leaders across the broader GTM organization, Product, and Engineering teams to deliver the voice-of-customer and drive a culture of customer-centricity.

• 
Product Feedback: Ensure we develop a feedback flywheel, turning customer insights into meaningful product enhancements and service optimizations.

What You Have

• 
Leadership Experience: You are a natural leader, with a proven background in leading high performing customer success teams within late-stage or post-IPO Enterprise SaaS organizations, with a specific emphasis on “Strategic”, “Large Enterprise / Enterprise”, and/or top-tier / lighthouse accounts with multi-million dollar spend.

• 
Strategic Acumen: Expertise in designing and executing customer success strategies that foster adoption, reduce churn, and promote expansion.

• 
Empathy and Influence: A leadership style characterized by empathy, with a proven track record in team development through hiring, coaching, and fostering talent.

• 
Outcome-Oriented: Exceptional ability to drive results through owning strategic initiatives, KPI reporting, and adept at navigating complex customer scenarios.

• 
Communication Mastery: Superior communication skills, capable of effectively engaging and influencing at all organizational levels both internally, and externally.

• 
Agility: Capacity to excel in a rapidly expanding, dynamic setting and swiftly adjust to evolving requirements.

• 
Innovation: A genuine passion for technology and innovation, constantly seeking novel solutions to complex challenges.

jobs.description:
As a Staff Engineer on the Data Platform Experience team, you'll help shape how Datadog engineering teams build, operate, and evolve products on the Observability Data Platform. You'll lead the design and delivery of shared platform capabilities that reduce developer friction, improve operational visibility, and enable engineering teams to move faster with confidence. This role combines deep distributed systems expertise with technical leadership across multiple teams, influencing platform strategy while remaining hands-on in the code. You'll have the opportunity to solve company-wide challenges spanning cost intelligence, operational tooling, platform health, and developer experience.

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.

What You'll Do:

  • Lead strategic engineering initiatives that improve how product teams build, operate, and evolve services on the Observability Data Platform.
  • Design and build scalable platform capabilities for cost intelligence, including cloud cost allocation, trend analysis, and optimization recommendations.
  • Develop operational intelligence and self-service tooling that helps engineering teams understand platform health, troubleshoot incidents, and improve operational efficiency.
  • Drive reusable platform services and developer workflows that increase engineering autonomy while reducing operational complexity across multiple products.
  • Provide technical leadership across teams by influencing architecture, mentoring engineers, and raising engineering standards through hands-on technical contributions.
  • Participate in the team's on-call rotation and continuously improve platform reliability, observability, and operational excellence.

Who You Are:

  • You have experience designing and building large-scale SaaS or cloud platforms with deep expertise in distributed systems.
  • You have strong software architecture and system design skills and have successfully led complex technical initiatives across multiple teams.
  • You have a platform engineering mindset and enjoy building reusable capabilities that enable other engineering organizations to move faster.
  • You are an effective communicator who can influence technical direction without direct authority and collaborate across organizational boundaries.
  • You have experience with backend technologies such as Java and Go, and distributed infrastructure including Kafka and Kubernetes
  • Experience with observability platforms, internal developer platforms, operational tooling, developer productivity solutions, or AI-powered engineering workflows is beneficial but not required.

Datadog values people from all walks of life. We know not everyone will meet all the above qualifications on day one. That’s okay. If you’re passionate about technology and want to grow your experience, we encourage you to apply.

jobs.title: Senior Applied Scientist - Behavior AI
jobs.description:
The Behavior AI team builds the AI-based anomaly detection behind Datadog's security products. Our models learn what normal looks like across the billions of logs, events, and telemetry records flowing through the platform every second, and they flag the behavior that does not fit, on every record, in real time, at a cost that makes sense at our scale. What we build does not ship to a single feature. The same models power detection across many of Datadog's security products at once, so the work has impact well beyond any one team. Large general-purpose models are too slow and too expensive to run in that path, so we take the opposite approach: small, custom models, designed for high-throughput stream processing and optimized to run cheaply on every record.

 

We are hiring a Senior Applied Scientist to build these models from start to finish. You will contribute to designing the architecture, training at scale, and the optimization work that takes a model from training to running efficiently on production traffic. This optimization requires a deep understanding of the constraints imposed by both the software and the hardware, together with the applied mathematics to work within them: often it comes down to finding a mathematical reformulation that fits those constraints better, and that judgment can decide whether a model reaches production at all.

 

The work involves a number of open questions. How do you obtain most of the quality of a large model from one that is far smaller and cheap enough to run on the full stream? Where is it worth trading exactness for speed, and how do you reason about the error you accept? How do you make a small model's outputs clear enough that the detection engineers and analysts who rely on it can trust what it reports? If these are the problems you want to work on, we would like to hear from you.

 

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture: the relationships and collaboration it builds, and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.

 

What You'll Do:

 

  • Design and build custom mid-size models for high-throughput stream processing, and train them at scale.

 

  • Optimize these models from start to finish, working across both the mathematics and the systems, often by finding mathematical reformulations that fit the hardware and software constraints better.

 

  • Build the training data pipelines the work depends on when they do not already exist, from the raw stream to a training-ready dataset.

 

  • Work with engineering to integrate models into production, with a clear focus on GPU utilization, latency, and cost per record on live traffic.

 

  • Plan the roadmap of model and system improvements, based on a solid understanding of the product and of what matters most to users.

 

  • Build an agentic layer on top of the models to analyze, validate, and act on their outputs.

 

  • Build lightweight interpretability tools that make model behavior easier to explain to the people who rely on it.

 

  • Maintain and monitor the models, services, and infrastructure your team owns, and take part in your team's on-call rotation.

 

Who You Are:

 

  • You have a BS/MS/PhD in Computer Science, Engineering, Machine Learning, Applied Mathematics, or a related scientific field, or equivalent experience.

 

  • You have hands-on experience training and fine-tuning models at scale, and deploying them into production systems with real throughput and cost constraints.

 

  • You have a working knowledge of how GPUs work, and a track record of making models run efficiently within real hardware constraints.

jobs.title: Senior Applied Scientist - AI Platform
jobs.description:
AI Platform builds the foundations of Datadog's AI efforts. The org is 70+ people organised in three pillars: training and serving (GPU clusters, distributed training, low-level infrastructure), agents (agent harnesses, memory systems, the internal AI gateway that routes every LLM request at Datadog), and evaluation and experimentation. This role sits in the evaluation and experimentation pillar, which owns Datadog's shared annotation and evaluation infrastructure — including the evaluation scenario store and the telemetry archival systems used across the Bits org. Together they let an agent travel back in time and query what Datadog looked like at the exact moment an incident happened, so scenarios can be replayed and agent performance tracked over time.

Specifically, you'll be the first applied scientist on GenSim (Generative Simulations), the team that builds the environments Datadog's agents learn in. GenSim doesn't replay sampled telemetry — it stands up real, fully instrumented applications that talk to Datadog, drives them with representative traffic, injects controlled failures, and records what happens. Because GenSim injected the failure, it knows the ground truth. That corpus — hundreds of postmortem-derived scenarios and thousands of runnable applications — is today the primary source of post-training data for Datadog's own SRE model, and the substrate that Bits AI SRE and our other agents are trained and evaluated against.

The team has no applied science support today and is learning post-training data methodology on the fly. That's the gap this role fills, and the open questions are the interesting part. How do you tell whether a generated environment is actually representative of the messy, incomplete telemetry real customers run — rather than a suspiciously clean one where every monitor exists and every service emits complete logs? How do you make injected problems genuinely hard, and how do you even measure difficulty? How do you define and control the quality of post-training data when correctness, representativeness and difficulty pull in different directions? How do you evaluate an agent end to end when the trajectory is non-deterministic? Creating simulated agent environments for monitoring and SRE work is not well solved in open source or in published research, and Datadog is the leading company in this field. If those are the problems you want to spend your time on, come build this with us.

What You'll Do:

  • Own the applied science direction for GenSim: set the methodology and the forward-looking technical calls on how simulated environments and post-training data should be built, on a team where that decision-making does not exist yet.
  • Define, measure and raise the quality of post-training data — basic correctness, representativeness against the real distribution of customer systems and production telemetry, and difficulty — and make those measures something the team can act on release over release.
  • Close the realism gap. Simulated environments today are too clean and the injected problems are not yet hard enough; you'll drive the research and the engineering that make them look like real, imperfect production systems.
  • Build scalable, production-grade systems rather than research scripts. The output is not just a dataset — it is a system of synthetic environments that must be reliable and invokable inside a training loop.
  • Determine how this data is best applied, in LLM post-training and in evaluation, and own the agent and LLM application evaluation approaches for these environments.
  • Work cross-functionally with the engineers and applied scientists on adjacent teams — Bits AI SRE, the model training effort, and the wider evaluation and experimentation pillar — so that what you learn moves freely in both directions.

Who You Are:

  • You have a PhD, MS or equivalent research experience in a scientific field, with strong applied mathematics grounding.
  • 6+ years of relevant applied science or ML engineering experience, including setting technical direction for others.
  • You have hands-on experience with LLM and agent post-training data: how it is created, managed, and how training-data quality is controlled. This is the requirement that matters most.
  • You have real domain expertise in LLMs and agentic applications — not classical ML fine-tuning. Fine-tuning classifiers or traditional models is a different problem from the one this team is solving.
  • You have evaluated agents or LLM applications, and can define what 'good' means before you measure it.
  • You are a strong programmer and production software engineer. Python at minimum, plus the ability to ship scalable production systems and work with distributed systems.
  • You collaborate well across engineering and science teams, and you're comfortable being the domain expert who decides what comes next.
  • You thrive in ambiguity and can make sound technical calls when the path isn't yet defined.

Bonus Points:

  • Hands-on LLM fine-tuning, post-training or model training experience.
  • Background in statistics, experiment design and data analysis.
  • Experience deploying production-level ML infrastructure.
  • Observability or monitoring systems background.
  • Architecture-level understanding of LLMs.

  • An inclusive company culture and the ability to join our Community Guilds

jobs.title: AI Research Scientist - Datadog AI Research (DAIR)
jobs.description:
As a Research Scientist on our team, you will partner with Research Engineers, working on fundamental research problems and collaborating with Datadog's product and engineering teams to translate research advances into products.

 

Building on our track record of AI-powered solutions (e.g., Bits AI, Bits Evolve, and our time series foundation model), Datadog AI Research tackles high-risk, high-reward problems grounded in real-world challenges in cloud observability and security.

 

We are focused on two research areas:

 

  1. World Models for Observability -- Training multimodal foundation models that learn the joint dynamics of distributed systems across metrics, traces, logs, topology, and events. These models power advanced forecasting, anomaly detection, root cause analysis, counterfactual simulation ("what if?"), and provide a learned planning backbone for our autonomous agents.
  2. Trained Agents for Observability -- Post-training models to operate autonomously across Datadog's domain. SRE incident response is our first target, with a clear path to code repair, security response, and infrastructure optimization. We build the simulation environments, RL training loops, and evaluation infrastructure needed to train agents that match or surpass frontier models at a fraction of the cost.

 

What You'll Do:

 

  • Conduct research in generative AI and machine learning, building specialized foundation models and trained agents for observability
  • Train multimodal models on large-scale, diverse telemetry data (metrics, logs, traces, topology, events) using distributed training infrastructure
  • Design and build simulated environments and RL training loops for on-policy agent training and evaluation
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams (Product, Engineering) to integrate capabilities like multimodal world modeling and autonomous agents into Datadog's products
  • Stay at the forefront of foundation models, world models, and RL-based agent research
  • Contribute to research publications, present at top-tier conferences (e.g., NeurIPS, ICLR, ICML), and help open-source key model artifacts and benchmarks

 

Who You Are:

 

  • You hold a PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, or a related field, with deep expertise in areas like generative modeling, world models, AI agents, reinforcement learning, or multimodal learning (or have equivalent experience)
  • You have extensive experience designing and implementing deep learning models and agents, with a strong background in distributed training frameworks (e.g., DeepSpeed, Megatron-LM) and ML libraries (PyTorch)
  • You have a track record of impactful publications at top-tier venues (e.g., NeurIPS, ICLR, ICML, TMLR)
  • You are familiar with efficient training, post-training, and inference techniques for large foundation models
  • You can explain complex models and research findings to both technical and non-technical audiences

 

Bonus Points (any of the following):

 

  • Experience bridging research and real-world product applications, especially with large foundation models, world models, or RL-trained agents
  • Passion for pushing the boundaries of AI with a focus on customer impact and scalable deployment
  • Experience writing production data pipelines and applications
  • Hands-on experience with GPU programming and optimization, including CUDA

 

Datadog values people from all walks of life. We understand not everyone will meet all the above qualifications on day one. That's okay. If you’re passionate about technology and want to grow your skills, we encourage you to apply.

  • Competitive global benefits

jobs.description:
What Cognite is: Relentless to achieve

Cognite operates at the forefront of industrial digitalization, building AI, and data solutions that solve the world’s hardest, highest-impact problems. With unmatched industrial heritage and a comprehensive suite of AI capabilities, including low-code AI agents, Cognite accelerates the digital transformation to drive operational improvements.

We thrive in challenges. We challenge assumptions. We execute with speed and ownership. If you view obstacles as signals to step forward - not backwards - you’ll feel right at home here. 

Our Moonshot is bold: Unlock $100B in customer value by 2035, and redefine how global industry works. Join us in this venture where AI and data meet ingenuity, and together, we will forge the path to a smarter, more connected industrial future.


 

About the Role

As a Deployment Strategist, you are the owner of the customer's problem and the value we promise to deliver. You are the bridge between a customer's business objective and our technical delivery team, accountable for the "why" and the "what", while Solution Architects and Data Engineers own the "how".

You will work with senior customer stakeholders to scope value, define pilots and releases, steer delivery through to go-live, and drive adoption so that value is actually realized after launch. You combine the discipline of a program manager with the product thinking of a field product owner, and you are as comfortable in a steering committee as you are in a working session with plant engineers.

This is a hands-on role. You are expected to shape the engagement, not just report on it.

What You'll Do

Scope and define value

  • Partner with Revenue to run discovery, map stakeholders, and translate business problems into a clearly scoped engagement (outcomes, MVP, success criteria, timeline, commercial boundaries).
  • Build value cases and success metrics with the customer, and keep them visible throughout delivery.
  • Define what "done" and "valuable" mean for each release, and manage scope against them.

Own delivery outcomes

  • Lead engagements end to end, from kickoff through go-live, using an iterative, continuous-delivery approach.
  • Prioritize the backlog with the customer and the delivery team, and make trade-off decisions on scope, timeline, and quality.
  • Manage risk, dependencies, and escalations across customer, partner, and internal teams, and unblock technical and political issues early.
  • Own delivery health: plan, margin, forecast, resourcing needs, and status reporting.

Drive adoption and value realization

  • Own the path from go-live to measurable usage: adoption plans, enablement and training, user feedback loops, and health indicators.
  • Identify blockers to adoption and expansion signals early, and act on them with the account team.
  • Prepare a clean handoff to the long-term run and support model.

Lead with partners and the team

  • Coordinate delivery with system integrator and partner teams, and protect clear accountability and contract boundaries.
  • Guide Solution Architects, Data Engineers, and Data Scientists in the engagement, and coach junior colleagues.
  • Contribute to the Value Delivery playbook: lessons learned, reusable templates, and delivery standards.

Feed the product

  • Turn field insight into structured product feedback for Product and Engineering.
  • Use AI tooling in your own work (analysis, documentation, reporting, prototyping) and help the team raise its standard.

What You Bring

Must have

  • 5+ years of experience in customer-facing delivery, program management or technical advisory for enterprise software or data/AI platforms.
  • A track record of owning complex, ambiguous engagements through to measurable customer outcomes.
  • Comfort with technical subject matter (data platforms, integration, cloud, analytics, or AI/ML). You do not need to build the solution, but you must understand it well enough to scope it and challenge it.
  • Executive-level communication: you can present, negotiate, and make decisions with senior customer stakeholders and with delivery engineers on the same day.
  • Strong command of agile and iterative delivery, backlog prioritisation, and scope management.
  • Fluent English and ideally French
  • Willingness to travel to customer sites up to 50%.

Nice to have

  • Experience in industrial sectors (energy, oil and gas, chemicals, pharma, manufacturing, utilities).
  • Experience with value-based scoping (ROI/TCO) and authoring product requirements or solution specifications.
  • Experience working in multi-vendor delivery models with system integrators.
  • Exposure to industrial data, knowledge graphs, or operational technology environments.
  • Experience in a high-growth software company or a "builder" role in a startup.
 
 
 
Learn more about us
 
 
 
  • Impact 2025
  • Cognite's Industrial AI: Moonshot
  • We’re globally recognized domain experts with an international presence that spans Phoenix, Houston, Oslo Tokyo, Bengaluru, and Abu Dhabi.

This is a hands-on, full-stack product role — you'll work across the whole product area, from the data model through to what users see on screen.

  • Translate French market requirements into clear specifications — turn the rules of the French energy market (including how device and meter data flows between grid operators and suppliers) into detailed product requirements covering compliance, data flows and data quality.
  • Build close working relationships — work hand in hand with key partners in the French market to understand their needs, shape requirements together, and build the kind of trusted relationship where they come to you first, using that closeness to steer what we build next for France.

  • Align global and local teams across all functions — partner closely with engineering, UX, QA and more, with full-stack influence, keeping everyone pointed at the right outcomes. Be the go-to person for this product area in France, and act as the link between our global and local teams to inform priorities and strategy.

About You

Ideally you'll have/be:

  • Proven experience as a Product Manager, Business Analyst, or equivalent role in software companies, with a strong track record of successfully localising complex software products for international markets
  • Previous experience in the French energy industry — you know how the market works and its key players (e.g. Enedis / GRDF), especially around device data and market flows. Experience with energy management or utility platforms in the French market is a strong plus.
  • Fluent in French and very comfortable in English — our platform and many of our teams operate in English, so you move easily between both.
  • Confident working directly with clients — you can run a working session with client stakeholders, draw out the real requirement behind the ask, and keep senior people aligned and brought in.
  • A builder's mentality — resourceful and hands-on, comfortable building a working prototype rather than waiting for the perfect specification.
  • Technically comfortable — at ease with data and data models, databases, and APIs, and able to prototype with modern AI tooling. You don't need to be an engineer, but you think like one and can hold your own in a technical conversation. Equally happy reasoning about a data model and about what the end user sees on screen.
  • A clear, sharp communicator — able to cut through noise and articulate technical and market complexity to a range of stakeholders, including clients.
  • Experience collaborating across cross-functional teams — engineering, QA, BA, Programme, Delivery etc — to deliver localised solutions.
  • Proficiency in AI tools throughout all stages of the product lifecycle — from discovery and ideation to delivery and iteration.

jobs.title: Acoustic Researcher
jobs.description:
Full-time · On-site (Paris Marseille)

The sea is the physical layer of the economy—the conduit for our energy, communications, and trade. It is also Europe’s exposed flank. Pelagon is building the answer.

Founded by Aymeric (serial deeptech entrepreneur; founded & exited Scortex, Leading AI solution for manufacturing quality) and Gauthier (Navy officer and McKinsey), Pelagon is building a foundational multimodal acoustic model for autonomous maritime protection (underwater and surface) in service of European sovereignty. It will be deployed on a distributed, autonomous network of vectors (UUVs, buoys, sailbuoys, seabed…) to provide real-time understanding of underwater threats.

France and Europe have world-class acoustic engineers and a long history in underwater warfare. By bridging this expertise with modern physical-AI strategies (as seen in autonomous driving and robotics). Europe is still missing it’s naval NeoPrime, Pelagon aims to become to lead the way in autonomous marine protection—from detection to interception—partnering with leading navies, primes, and neo-primes, while also operating its own fleet as a service.

Pelagon is backed by Hexa, the pioneer startup studio in Europe, which has launched 35+ companies, including unicorns like Front, Aircall, and Spendesk, combining €230m+ ARR and €750m raised.

Why this matters

The sea is the physical layer of the economy — and Europe's most exposed flank. Everything that moves beneath the surface leaves an acoustic trace, but the ocean is a brutal channel: multipath, ambient noise, shifting propagation. Reading it is first and foremost a physics problem.

France and Europe have a world-class heritage in underwater acoustics and sonar. Pelagon's bet is to bridge that science with modern physical-AI strategies and a distributed fleet of UUVs, buoys, sailbuoys and seabed sensors. As our Acoustic Researcher, you are the physics backbone of that system — the person who understands underwater sound deeply enough that our models can learn from it. You partner directly with our AI Engineers, who consume the features, representations and data you help define.

What you'll do

• 
Model underwater sound propagation across realistic ocean environments to enable our synthetic data generation pipeline.

• 
Characterize and classify acoustic signatures of surface and underwater targets; build the ground-truth understanding our multimodal acoustic model is trained against.

• 
Design and reason about sensor and array geometries: what to deploy, where, and how to extract maximum information from constrained & distributed vectors.

• 
Work hand in hand with AI Engineers on physics-constrained learning strategies ans models.

What we look for

• 
Deep grounding in underwater acoustics, sonar, or a closely related field (ocean acoustics, radar/array processing, acoustic signal processing). PhD or equivalent research experience.

• 
Strong command of statistical signal processing: detection & estimation theory, array processing, time-frequency analysis.

• 
Fluent in Python (NumPy/SciPy) for modeling, simulation and analysis; comfortable working with large datasets.

• 
A builder's instinct, you want your work deployed at sea, not left in a paper. Bias toward validating ideas against real data.

• 
Bonus: prior experience using machine learning on acoustic signals, naval / defense domain experience.

Why join now

• 
Founding ownership. You'll be one of the first engineers and will define the technical foundation of the company. Meaningful equity comes with that.

• 
A mission with weight. This is hardware that protects critical infrastructure and Europe's maritime space.

• 
Real things, in the real ocean, fast. You'll see your work in the water within weeks, not years.

• 
AI-first, at the edge, in the real world. We train our own models and run them where it counts: in the water, on the device. You'll be solving the edge-ML and power problems most companies only talk about.

• 
A sovereign, European deeptech at the inflection point of a market with strong NATO and EU policy momentum behind it.

jobs.title: Staff Machine Learning Engineer, LLM Inference Optimization
jobs.description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

Role Summary

Nebius Token Factory is building production-grade inference for open-source, customer, and internally optimized models. This role owns the path from model artifact to fast, reliable, cost-efficient endpoint. The work sits at the intersection of model internals, inference engines, serving architecture, benchmarking, and production deployment.

 

What You Will Do

  • Own a platform-level optimization pillar such as quantization, speculative decoding, KV-cache optimization, engine selection, or long-context serving.

  • Create reusable evaluation, benchmarking, and rollout frameworks across multiple model families.

  • Provide technical direction to MLEs, Applied Scientists, GPU kernel engineers, and infrastructure engineers on shared performance goals.

  • Optimize LLM and VLM endpoints for latency, throughput, memory efficiency, GPU utilization, quality, and cost per token.

  • Deploy, configure, benchmark, and extend inference engines such as vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, Triton Inference Server, NVIDIA Dynamo, or similar systems.

  • Build and productionize model-compression workflows, including quantization, quantization-aware training, distillation, low-bit serving, and accuracy recovery.

  • Implement or integrate speculative decoding, draft-model approaches, KV-cache optimization, prefix caching, chunked prefill, continuous batching, and disaggregated prefill/decode serving.

  • Build reproducible benchmark harnesses for TTFT, TPOT, tokens per second per GPU, p95/p99 latency, GPU memory, reliability, and cost per token.

  • Partner with GPU kernel engineers and platform engineers to diagnose bottlenecks across model code, kernels, runtime, scheduler, gateway, and cluster layers.

  • Write clear design docs, performance reports, rollout plans, and customer-facing technical explanations.

Required Qualifications

  • Strong Python and PyTorch engineering skills.

  • Hands-on experience deploying or optimizing LLM, VLM, or high-throughput transformer inference systems.

  • Practical knowledge of at least one modern inference stack such as vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, Triton Inference Server, NVIDIA Dynamo, Ray Serve, KServe, or equivalent internal systems.

  • Strong understanding of transformer inference bottlenecks, including KV cache, attention, memory bandwidth, batching, parallelism, and long-context serving.

  • Ability to reason quantitatively about latency, throughput, quality, utilization, and cost tradeoffs.

  • Strong communication skills and ability to collaborate with research, kernel, infrastructure, product, and customer teams.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with quantization-aware training, post-training quantization, FP8, INT8, INT4, NVFP4, MXFP4, AWQ, GPTQ, SmoothQuant, or related techniques.

  • Experience with distillation, speculative decoding, EAGLE, Medusa, multi-token prediction, or other inference acceleration methods.

  • Experience with agentic workloads, including tool calling, structured outputs, streaming APIs, high concurrency, and multi-step orchestration.

  • CUDA or Triton familiarity, even if the role is not

jobs.title: Intelligence Center X Engineering Manager - EMEA
jobs.description:
Build and lead the team that brings Intelligence Center X to life for leading companies across the EMEA, through business-relevant enterprise agentic AI use cases.

About Intelligence Center X

Intelligence Center X (ICX) is Siemens' industrial AI platform. ICX combines Siemens' own core graph, ontology, machine learning and agentic AI technology with our industrial software foundations to bring truly differentiated capabilities to market. It connects a company's enterprise and operational data into an enterprise ontology, and uses machine learning and agentic AI to reason over it and act on it.

Our customers are leaders in automotive, aerospace and defense, semiconductors and electronics, industrial machinery, pharma and financial services.

How we engage with customers

Beyond typical demos, we work forward-deployed with the customer — on relevant data, against their problem — and build a working agentic AI solution, grounded in an enterprise ontology. It is how we establish value with customers: where they see the use case come to life, and where we earn the right to move forward.

Key Responsibilities

The role

As the ICX Engineering Manager for the EMEA, you build and lead the EMEA team of ICX Engineers — a presales FDE team that leads the ideation and creation of these engagements. They model a customer's domain as an enterprise ontology, build agents and machine learning that reason over it and act on it, and deliver working agentic applications that compel customers to invest in Intelligence Center X with Siemens.

This is a formal people-management role, and a player-coach one. You:

• Lead by example — build customer solutions yourself, and set the bar for how the team builds them.

• Are a senior presence on key opportunities — with customers, and alongside sales leadership.

• Recruit and grow the team — hire strong engineers, and develop them.

• Evolve the global practice — work with global ICX leaders on how we engage with customers across every zone.

You work alongside sales teams and strategic partners, and report to the EMEA Pre-Sales Leader.

What your team's work looks like

In a given week, one of your engineers is connecting quality and supplier data for an aerospace manufacturer to find why defects keep reaching its customers. Another is building an agentic assistant that helps a pharma company make batch release decisions in hours rather than days. You are with a third customer's leadership team, shaping the next engagement. Your job is to make sure each one lands — and that what one engineer learns, the next one starts with.

Requirements

Who you are

• You lead technical teams that work with customers. Through formal management or team-lead roles, you have led customer-facing FDE, presales, services or other technical teams.

• You are hands-on with agentic AI and ontology. You still build, and your team follows your example.

• You are entrepreneurial. You take ownership, move at startup pace and find a route to an outcome before the problem is fully defined — with some of the largest companies in the world.

• You think in business value, and you are credible with customers and sales leadership alike.

Skills and experience

We look for experience or strong potential in the following areas.

• Leading technical teams — formal management or team-lead roles for customer-facing FDE, presales, services or other technical teams.

• Technical consulting leadership — leading client engagements and delivery teams in agentic AI, data and analytics at a consultancy or systems integrator.

• Agentic development tools — Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot or similar, used to build quickly and well.

• Enterprise ontology — modelling a real business domain as an ontology or knowledge graph and putting it to work in an enterprise.

• Machine learning and data science — building models that solve real business problems, such as forecasting, anomaly detection or classification.

• Experience in our industries — manufacturing, engineering, supply chain, pharma, aerospace or financial services.

Some travel is expected, up to 25%. For people who want to spend even more time on site with customers, there is room for it.

Why Join Us

• Grow with ICX. Lead as Siemens brings Intelligence Center X to the market as a leading industrial AI platform.

• Build and lead a team. ICX Engineering is growing fast, and you shape both the Americas team and the global practice.

• The problem every enterprise is working on. Agentic AI grounded in a company's own data and context.

jobs.description:
Werk jij graag op het snijvlak van data, (administratieve) processen en onderwijs? Houd je van structuur, maar kun je ook snel schakelen wanneer de situatie daarom vraagt? Taken

Wij zijn een taal- en inburgeringsschool die onder andere werkt met gemeentelijke opdrachtgevers. Dat betekent dat zorgvuldige registratie, rapportage en kwaliteitsborging essentieel zijn. In deze functie speel jij daarin een centrale rol. Je takenpakket bestaat uit drie hoofdlijnen: rapportages & analyses, functioneel beheer van het cursistvolgsysteem (CVS) en beheer van administratieve instructies. Jij zorgt er samen met uitvoerders voor dat er heldere instructies zijn voor administratieve taken en het gebruik van het cursistvolgsysteem, jij signaleert het als instructies niet worden opgevolgd, analyseert waar het manco zit en verbetert. Aan de andere kant hou je contact met het management en adviseer en denk je mee over gewenste wijzigingen in administratie ten behoeve van kwaliteit, rapportages en efficiëntie in de organisatie. Jij vertaalt wensen van uitvoerders en wensen van het management naar mogelijke verbeteringen in het cursistvolgsysteem en onderhoudt hierover contact met de ICT’er. En tot slot maak jij periodieke rapportages voor gemeenten en maak je analyses en rapportages op aanvraag. 

In grotere organisaties zijn deze taken verdeeld over meerdere functies. Bij ons krijg jij het overzicht én het vertrouwen.

In deze rol

• Je hebt minimaal een afgeronde opleiding op HBO niveau

Benefits
