jobs.title: Senior MLOps Engineer, Buyer
jobs.description:
Brief info about Vinted 

Our mission is to make second-hand the first choice, and we're looking for people who want to help us get there. Every day, we work together to help our members buy and sell pre-loved clothing and lifestyle items, giving each piece a second life – or even a third.
The Vinted Group is made up of three business units that support this mission:

Vinted Marketplace is Europe’s leading platform for second-hand fashion and a go-to destination for all kinds of pre-loved items, with a growing range of categories. Our platform connects millions of members across 20+ markets, helping great items find a new life.

Vinted Go enhances the shipping experience with a vast network of over 500,000 pick-up and drop-off points, partnering with more than 60 carriers across Europe, with added services like item verification for peace of mind on high-value pieces.

Vinted Pay is the newest part of the Vinted Group, dedicated to bringing secure, reliable payments to buyers and sellers across Europe. Seamlessly integrated into the Vinted app, it helps keep every transaction safe, efficient, and easy for our members.

Founded in 2008 in Lithuania, Vinted began as a way for friends to find new homes for clothes they no longer needed. In 2019, we became Lithuania's first unicorn! Today, our headquarters remain in Vilnius, and we've grown with offices across Europe, supported by a team of over 2,000 people. 

Information about the position 

The Buyer domain's Data Science teams build and iterate on our most critical ML systems—like ranking, retrieval, and recommendations—that serve millions of users. As our ambition and the complexity of these models grow, we are scaling our MLOps capabilities to match: 

We are hiring an MLOps Engineer to solve this. This is a high-impact "bridge" role, not to build new platforms, but to be the expert user of our existing platforms (GCP/Vertex AI, Vespa, Triton). Your mission is to take our Data Science team's work, rectify the current ad-hoc solutions, and build the robust, automated, and high-quality "path-to-production" our advanced models require.

Also by joining Vinted, you’ll become part of an active community of engineers who are keen on sharing knowledge, organizing learning workshops and so much more!

In this position, you’ll 

  • Productionise ML models: be responsible for migrating all existing model training code from experimental or proof-of-concept stages to robust and automated pipelines.
  • Build continuous training (CT) pipelines: design, build, and maintain automated workflows for data preparation, model training, and batch scoring.
  • Automate model serving & integration: package and deploy traditional ML models (e.g., in ONNX format) to our existing serving infrastructure, primarily Vespa and/or Triton.
  • Close the deployment loop: automate model deployments where they are still manual. For example, building a GitHub Action that deploys a new model to Vespa, triggered by a webhook from a successful Vertex AI training pipeline.
  • Build the missing quality gates: build the automated quality and evaluation gates that our pipelines lack today. This includes:
  • Establish and uphold ML Model Lifecycle Standards: Take ownership of and continuously improve the standards, quality, and governance of the complete ML model lifecycle

About you 

  • We are looking for an "ML-literate" Software Engineer, not a Data Scientist. You are a builder and an automator with a strong service mindset.
  • Must-have technical skills: deep expertise in GCP/Vertex AI (or equivalents like SageMaker), Kubernetes, and Docker.
  • Automation expertise: proven experience building robust CI/CD and automation pipelines (e.g., GitHub Actions, Jenkins, etc.).
  • ML-Literate: you understand ML workflows and concepts (training, evaluation, inference) well enough to debug pipelines and build meaningful quality gates.
  • Soft skills: a strong "service mindset," excellent communication, and the ability to act as a bridge between the highly technical worlds of Data Science and Infrastructure. You are pragmatic and driven to get high-quality work into production.
  • Bonus Points: familiarity with ML serving platforms like Vespa search engine or NVIDIA Triton and model formats like ONNX.
  • Willingness to learn and master new technologies and concepts.
  • We value pragmatism, big-picture thinking, curiosity, and problem-solving skills.

Work perks 

  • The opportunity to benefit from our share options programme
  • 30 days of paid annual leave
  • Newest MacBook models
  • Confidential Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for you and your family
  • Home office support: we provide IT workstation equipment and a personal budget of up to €540 for home workplace furniture
  • Lunch benefit per your workday
  • Frequent team-building events
  • A personal monthly budget for shopping on Vinted
  • Access to a discounted gym membership plan
  • Pension Plan with Vinted matching 150% of your chosen contribution
  • Supplemental Private Health Insurance
  • Life and Disability insurance
  • A subsidised Deutschlandticket for your commute to the office by public transport
  • A dog-friendly office

Working at Vinted 

Workation policy

Better balance holidays with workdays by working remotely! Up to 90 days per year in the EU, of these, 21 days can be spent globally. For non-EU citizens, it's 21 days worldwide. This can be combined with time off for vacation or personal time.

Individual learning budget

Each year, you’ll be given a learning budget (starting at €3,000), and a total of up to 10 working days over a 2-year period to support your personal and professional development.

Hybrid work

jobs.description:
WHO WE ARE 

Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.

Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.

Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.

BY JOINING OUR TEAM YOU’LL GET TO

• 
Build the machine that builds the machine. Join TechOps at the forefront of advanced manufacturing, we’re building the production system that will enable commercial fusion. The Production lines, tooling, and processes are being developed from the ground up; you'll create the ways of working, not inherit them.

• 
Work at the frontier of manufacturing technology. Bring your creativity to evaluate, qualify, and deploy processes with no industry playbook, every component you build and every process you shape goes directly into the core of the stellarator magnet technology.

• 
Do work that matters, and see it grow. The hardware you build is the product and your career grows with it, from prototyping and process development through quality and industrialization, alongside exceptional colleagues from around the world.

• 
Make an impact you can point to. In a small, fast-moving team, your calls on equipment, quality, and process directly shape how a world-class deep-tech company produces superconducting magnets with results visible on the shop floor, not buried in a slidedeck.

YOUR IMPACT

You keep Alpha's cost and schedule baselines honest against each other. Without a credible risk register and change process, changes slip into the program outside any controlled path, the IMS and cost forecast quietly drift apart, and a gate review surprises leadership with numbers nobody signed off on. Your job is to prevent that by making risk and change management a live, trusted function from the earliest stage of delivery, rather than something bolted on once problems have compounded.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

• 
Establish and maintain the Alpha risk register across infrastructure, manufacturing and machine workstreams, facilitating structured risk identification, assessment and assignment of mitigation owners

• 
Own the change control process end to end, from intake and schedule, cost and technical impact assessment through to approval routing and the change log, working closely with the Cost Controller and Programme Schedule Manager so all baselines reflect the same accepted changes

• 
Prepare risk-adjusted inputs for release gate decisions, including quantified schedule and cost exposure and mitigation status

• 
Run regular risk reviews with workstream owners and escalate emerging risks early, before they reach senior leadership as surprises

• 
Build risk and change governance standards that scale as Alpha and Stellaris grow in parallel, with different partners and delivery models

• 
Support the PMO's wider reporting cadence alongside the PMO Analyst/Coordinator

WHO YOU ARE

• 
Experienced in risk and change management on major capital programs in energy, industrial, research infrastructure or similarly complex multi-discipline settings

• 
Able to build a risk and change framework from scratch, not just administer an inherited one; you know what good governance looks like before it exists

• 
Confident holding the line on change discipline with internal engineers and external partners who have their own priorities, combining analytical rigor with the communication skills to make it stick

• 
Comfortable working with high autonomy while program structure is still being built

• 
Fluent in English; German is a strong advantage given the contractor and regulatory landscape

• 
Familiar with AI tools and digital ways of working, and quick to adapt in a lean, fast-paced environment

INTERVIEW PROCESS

• 
Recruiter Interview (30-60 min)

• 
Technical Screening (30 min)

• 
Technical Panel (3x60 min)

jobs.description:
At idealo, we've built a strong SEO foundation. Now, we're looking to take the next step. As AI-powered search experiences such as ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Perplexity, and Gemini increasingly influence how people research products and make purchasing decisions, we want to ensure idealo becomes a trusted and frequently cited source within these new shopping journeys.

As our GEO Manager, you'll take ownership of developing Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) as an additional growth discipline alongside our established SEO activities. Combining your technical SEO expertise with hands-on experience in AI search optimization, you'll develop our GEO strategy, establish meaningful visibility monitoring, and drive experimentation to understand what makes content and data discoverable, relevant, and citable by generative AI systems.

You'll work closely with our SEO team and collaborate across Product, Engineering, Content, Brand, and Communications to turn emerging opportunities into scalable solutions.

About your new role

• 
GEO Strategy & Development: You develop and drive idealo's GEO strategy and experimentation roadmap, building on our existing SEO foundation. You identify opportunities across generative search platforms and AI-assisted shopping journeys, translating emerging developments into actionable initiatives aligned with our broader SEO and business objectives.

• 
AI Visibility & Performance Monitoring: You establish and continuously improve a GEO monitoring framework covering platforms such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, and Google AI Overviews. You define relevant KPIs, including mention and citation rates, share of voice, sentiment, and positioning within AI-generated answers, and develop dashboards that make performance and progress transparent to different stakeholders.

• 
Technical GEO Optimization: You leverage your technical SEO expertise to improve how generative AI systems discover, interpret, and reference idealo's content. This includes optimizing structured data (Schema.org), semantic relationships, product and offer information, and identifying technical opportunities to strengthen our visibility and accessibility across AI-powered search experiences.

• 
Experimentation & Competitive Analysis: You design, implement, and evaluate GEO experiments, analyze idealo's visibility against relevant competitors, and translate findings into concrete optimization measures. You continuously assess emerging GEO tools, methodologies, and platform capabilities to improve our approach.

AI Shopping & Content Optimization: You explore how idealo's product, pricing, and offer data can become a valuable information source for AI agents and agentic commerce. Together with Content Marketing, you assess existing content and develop answer-focused, well-structured formats that strengthen relevance, authority, and citation potential.

• 
Cross-functional Collaboration & Knowledge Sharing: You connect technical SEO and GEO requirements with Product and Engineering initiatives and collaborate with Brand and Communications/PR on authority-building and digital PR opportunities. You actively share your expertise, communicate findings to stakeholders, and contribute insights from the evolving AI search landscape to idealo's long-term SEO strategy.

Skills & Requirements

• 
3-5 years of hands-on SEO experience, with a clear focus on technical SEO. 

• 
Strong technical SEO fundamentals: site architecture, crawlability, indexing, Core Web Vitals, JavaScript SEO, and experience running full technical audits. 

• 
Practical understanding of how generative search systems retrieve, summarize, and cite content.

• 
Experience with data analysis, KPI definition, and translating data into recommendations. 

• 
Hands-on proficiency with core SEO tools (Google Search Console, GA4, Ahrefs or Semrush, Screaming Frog or similar crawler). 

• 
Familiarity with structured data, semantic models, and entity-based SEO. 

• 
Experience with GEO/AI visibility tools (e.g., Profound, AirOps, Rankscale, Peec AI, Otterly). 

• 
Strong AI mindset: willing to test new GEO tools and methods and share learnings with the team. 

• 
Excellent communication skills, able to present technical findings clearly to non-technical stakeholders across Engineering, Product, Content, Brand, and Communications/PR. 

• 
Experience in e-commerce, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, SQL or reporting automation with tools such as n8n are a plus.

At idealo you can expect

• 
You want to further your education? We take your personal development goals seriously and, in addition to our idealo Learning Hub, eLearning offerings (e.g., Udemy), coaching & mediation, we also offer you the opportunity to benefit individually from additional learning and development budget.

Our office in the heart of Berlin offers free organic breakfast, excellent free lunch (vegan and vegetarian), as well as free coffee, lemonades and after-work beer, in addition to the "standard foosball". jobs.title: Engineering Manager – Control & Low-Level Software (m/f/d)
jobs.description:
About the Role at RobCo

RobCo is building the category of Autonomous Industrial Robotics and we're doing it fast. We believe that automating the ordinary frees humans to do the extraordinary, and we're building the end-to-end robotics infrastructure to make that possible - hardware, software, and AI in one stack that just works. 

At RobCo, we don’t just build robots, we are redefining the relationship between hardware and AI. Our end-to-end solutions seamlessly combine advanced, scalable industrial hardware with a central software suite powered by Physical AI to make manufacturing truly autonomous, efficient, and scalable. By delivering field-ready robotic solutions that just work, we empower industrial companies to automate without complexity and successfully solve the global labor shortage.

At RobCo, we automate the ordinary, so humans can do the extraordinary. To achieve this, we are looking for an ambitious Engineering Manager - Control & Low-Level Software (m/f/d) to help us establish RobCo as a leading provider of automation solutions.

In this key role, you will lead the team behind how our robots move: RobControl, the real-time controller running on every RobCo robot, together with control unit software, robot modeling and hardware integration. One controller codebase drives our modular robots, OEM configurations and Alfie, our autonomous industrial robot, so your team's work reaches every robot in the field. Managing a team of control, embedded and software engineers, you will balance new capabilities for Alfie and our physical AI roadmap with the reliability factory customers expect on every shift.

Your Responsibilities

• 
Own the hardware-software bridge: Lead the team developing our real-time controller, robot models, hardware interfacing via EtherCat, as well as core robot algorithms like motion generation and planning, calibration, etc., running on Linux-based Control Units.

• 
Lead and Grow the Team: Act as a people-first leader for a mixed team of experienced engineers and early-career talent. Hire and coach, and balance roadmap work with field support through clear priorities and a fair on-call rotation.

• 
Drive Engineering Excellence: Set standards for code quality, hardware-in-the-loop and automated testing, and CI/CD, so that done means tested, released and running in the field. Improve observability so field issues can be diagnosed remotely and quickly.

• 
One Platform for Every Robot: Keep one controller codebase for modular robots, OEM configurations and Alfie, extending it to new kinematic structures, more joints and multi-arm systems without forking it. Manage technical debt and architectural health as we scale.

• 
Partner Across Teams: Work with Product Management, Hardware, Safety & Compliance and Robot Intelligence to turn customer and autonomy needs into a clear roadmap, integrate RobControl with the safety controller, and support certification against ISO 10218 and ISO 13849.

• 
Cross-Team Leadership: Mentor junior EMs and help evolve company-wide engineering best practices and software-first principles.

We're looking for someone who has:

• 
Completed a university degree in Robotics, Mechatronics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering or a related field.

• 
3+ years of experience leading engineering teams that ship real-time or embedded software for robots, motion systems or other industrial machines.

• 
Deep experience in robot control and motion is a big plus: kinematics and dynamics, trajectory generation, and position, velocity and torque control. Strong C++ and Python on real-time Linux, with hands-on EtherCAT and ROS 2 experience.

• 
Proven track record of driving an AI-first engineering culture and implementing agentic workflows that measurably accelerate team velocity and system efficiency.

• 
Expert knowledge of modern SDLC practices for software that runs on hardware, including hardware-in-the-loop testing and staged releases, with a track record of improving release frequency and field stability.

•

jobs.title: Technical Product Manager, Integrations
jobs.description:
Who we are

Foundation models transformed text and images. Structured data - the largest and most consequential data format in the world - stayed untouched, until now. What LLMs did for language, we're doing for tables.

We pioneered tabular foundation models: TabPFN v2 was a Nature cover story, has passed 3.5M+ downloads and 7,500+ GitHub stars, and runs in production from detecting lung disease with Oxford Cancer Analytics to preventing train failures with Hitachi. The hardest problems - millions of rows, real-time inference, entirely new modalities - are still open, and no one else is working on them at this level.

We're a small, highly selective team of 40+ with backgrounds from Google, DeepMind, Meta, Apple, Amazon, Jane Street, and CERN, led by Frank Hutter, Noah Hollmann, and Sauraj Gambhir, and advised by Bernhard Schölkopf and Turing Award winner Yann LeCun.

In July 2026, less than 18 months after our €9M pre-seed, we joined SAP as an independent frontier AI lab - same team, mission, and open-weights models, now backed by more than €1 billion over four years.

The role

Most enterprises will never call our API directly. They will meet TabPFN inside the platforms they already run: SAP, AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Databricks, or their own cloud. How well that works, how fast each release arrives there, and which platforms come next is the job of our Technical Product Manager for Integrations.

You take each model release from handover to live across every channel, working with the engineers who build the model and the partner teams who host it. Inside SAP you carry the product side of TabPFN across its platforms, from AI Core to SAP Analytics Cloud, and you help build the integration engineering team that will work with you. Several decisions are yours to bring to the table: which announced channels we build next, what a marketplace listing should cost, how support for all of this works.

You work directly with our product team, our engineers and the founders, and you report to the CTO. This suits someone who enjoys landing things on a date as much as deciding what to build, and who still likes being close to the code.

What you'll do

• 
Take every model release live across SAP, the cloud marketplaces and customer environments, on a plan you build with product and engineering.

• 
Be the technical counterpart for the partner teams that host TabPFN, from SAP's platform teams to the hyperscaler marketplaces.

• 
Shape how TabPFN shows up inside SAP's stack and what the integration engineering team builds first.

• 
Bring the open channel decisions to the founders with a recommendation, and stay hands-on: listings, docs, smoke tests, a PR when it is faster than asking.

What we're looking for

• 
Two or more years as product manager for a platform or integration surface: a product that ships into partners' platforms, or that other companies build on.

• 
You have shipped through gates you did not control, landed multi-team releases on dates, and made a large enterprise's process work for a small, fast team.

• 
You started as an engineer and never fully stopped: you read code, logs and scan reports without a translator.

• 
You are in Berlin or ready to relocate; Freiburg or New York can work.

What sets you apart

• 
You have shipped into an SAP, Salesforce, Microsoft or Oracle ecosystem, or know the cloud marketplaces from the inside.

• 
You have deployed machine learning models and know what GPUs cost.

• 
You have worked at a startup, and you use AI tools to take real work off your plate.

Life at Prior Labs

You'll work alongside researchers and builders who hold themselves to a very high bar - in the quality of their work and in how they work with each other. We move fast and still take the time to do things right.

Our teams are based in Berlin, Freiburg, and New York - when you're working on something as hard as TabPFN, being in the same room matters. Wherever you're based, the whole company comes together regularly for offsites to build and celebrate together.

The best products and teams are built by people with a wide range of perspectives and backgrounds. We welcome applications from all identities and walks of life - especially if you've ever felt discouraged by "not checking every box" - and provide equal opportunities regardless of gender, sexual orientation, origin, disability, or any other trait that makes you who you are.

jobs.title: Research Software Engineering Intern (f/m/d)
jobs.description:
Description

QuantumDiamonds is building the world’s first commercial quantum sensing tools for chip failure analysis. As our Research Software Engineering Intern in Pre-Development, you bring our measurement software together. A measurement protocol is the recipe our Quantum Diamond Microscope (QDm) follows for one measurement: how laser, microwaves and camera are sequenced and timed, and how raw camera frames become a magnetic field image of a chip. Our engineers write new protocols whenever they test a new idea, and several backends for running them grew in parallel. You turn them into one shared Python framework that our engineers extend.

The challenge is a framework R&D still uses long after your internship: flexible enough that a new protocol is a day’s work, automated enough that a measurement runs without someone watching it, and structured enough that the next engineer extends it without reading all of it. An experienced colleague from the team mentors you and sets the architecture; you make that trade-off real in code, working with Claude Code every day, as our engineers do.

This is a full-time internship for 6 months, during or after your studies, starting as soon as possible.

Who we are

Founded in 2022 as a spin-off of TU Munich, QD leverages quantum sensors to rapidly capture three-dimensional current maps within multi-layer chips. Our strong, international team of over 70, including physicists, engineers, data scientists, and other experts, works side by side with major semiconductor manufacturers, supporting chip debugging and accelerating yield analysis. Backed by top-tier deep tech investors, semiconductor experts, and strategic public programs, we have ensured long-term stability, shifting from breakthrough to scale - and shaping the next chapter in chip testing.

Why join QuantumDiamonds?

Picture this:

• 
Quantum sensors that see inside the most advanced chips on Earth, right where two frontier fields collide.

• 
Nobel-Prize physics aimed at real customers with real problems, in production now, not someday.

• 
Physicists, data scientists, and engineers building side by side, turning deep science into tools the industry actually runs on.

• 
An international team that runs at hard problems for fun, where knowledge moves fast and so do you.

Still unsure about why joining us?

• 
You'll get to build a company together with a brilliant and welcoming team on a product that has never been done before.

• 
From Day 1, you'll own your own topics end to end and see the direct impact of your work on how the world sees QuantumDiamonds.

• 
Our technology is the cutting edge of tomorrow, starting today and not in 10 years.

• 
You’ll be part of a high-growth company backed by top-tier investors.

Let’s make the invisible visible!

What will you do

• 
Bring the measurement software of Pre-Development together into one shared Python framework, to a target architecture your mentor defines, and migrate the existing measurement protocols onto it.

• 
Keep the CI/CD pipeline on GitHub Actions healthy as the framework grows: tests, linting, packaging, releases.

• 
Give first-pass reviews on pull requests from our engineers (tests, conventions, API conformance) before your mentor approves them.

• 
Help our engineers extend the stack: new measurement protocols become modules in the framework, and you validate the migrated ones on our QDm systems together with them.

• 
Document the framework and hand it over so the team runs it on its own after your internship.

What is expected of you

• 
Enrolled in or recently graduated from a degree program in computer science, software engineering, computational engineering, physics or electrical engineering with a strong software focus.

• 
Available full time for 6 months, starting as soon as possible.

• 
Python is your working language: you structure packages, write type hints and tests, and have refactored or consolidated code you did not write.

• 
Git and CI are routine for you, and you know how to make hardware-dependent code testable: mocked instruments, recorded data and simulation, with runs on real hardware as a separate stage.

• 
AI coding agents are part of how you work, and you check their output the way you check your own.

• 
You review code and take review well, you can agree on a common interface with engineers who each prefer their own solution, and you treat your colleagues as your users.

• 
Fluent in English. On-site in Munich.

Experience with instrument control or lab automation in Python, with frameworks such as qudi, QCoDeS or PyMeasure, or contributions to open-source projects are a plus, not required. What we want you to bring is the patience to read code you did not write and the discipline to leave it better structured than you found it.

Our benefits

• 
Mission: At QD, we’re driven by more than just building great products - we aim to make a lasting difference. Joining us means contributing to meaningful work that goes beyond business as usual.

• 
Impact & growth: This is an exciting stage of our journey, and your voice matters. You’ll have the chance to shape our culture, influence key decisions, and grow alongside a company that’s scaling fast.

• 
Mentoring: An experienced colleague from the team mentors you throughout your internship.

• 
Health & fitness: With a company-sponsored Wellpass membership, you’ll have access to countless gyms, classes, and wellness offers across Germany to stay healthy and active.

• 
Team & culture: We believe the best ideas come when we connect outside the office. From regular off-sites to team events, you’ll be part of a collaborative and supportive environment.

• 
Well-being & balance: We value rest and recovery. That’s why you’ll enjoy 24 vacation days plus public holidays to recharge and return inspired.

About us

QuantumDiamonds GmbH, headquartered in Munich, Germany, develops and manufactures semiconductor inspection systems based on quantum sensing. Spun out of the Technical University of Munich in 2022, the company uses nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond to map electrical current with micrometer precision inside advanced 2.5D and 3D chip architectures. Nine of the world's ten largest semiconductor manufacturers are engaged with QuantumDiamonds, with systems deployed across Europe, the United States, and Asia. The company is investing €152 million to build the world's first production facility for quantum sensing-based semiconductor inspection tools, supported under the European Chips Act.

Mission

Turn operational needs, customer feedback, and product direction into clear product specifications—and then drive those capabilities through decisions, design, development, and validation.

You will work directly with the Head of Product on Legion and become a core contributor to both defining the product and running the process around it.

What You’ll Own

• 
Create clear, detailed product specifications for new features and capabilities.

• 
Take customer needs, operator feedback, technical constraints, and product direction and turn them into actionable product requirements.

• 
Own bounded features from early definition through design, development, feedback, and validation.

• 
Work directly with Product Design to translate specifications into detailed workflows and Figma designs.

• 
Review designs and implementations against product intent and requirements.

• 
Facilitate product discussions with government customers, third-party contractors, operators, engineers, and internal stakeholders.

• 
Prepare agendas and clearly identify topics requiring feedback, decisions, or alignment.

• 
Capture decisions, unresolved issues, customer feedback, and action items.

• 
Incorporate meeting outcomes directly into product specifications and related artifacts.

• 
Maintain feature status, decision history, feedback registers, and key product commitments.

• 
Identify ambiguity, conflicting requirements, and missing decisions before they slow the team down.

• 
Track important product and contractual deliverables.

• 
Help prepare product reviews, demonstrations, and customer discussions.

• 
Create enough structure to keep the organization aligned without introducing unnecessary process.

What Great Looks Like

You are given a problem such as:

“Operators need a better way to understand and respond to vehicle health issues during degraded communications.”

You meet with the relevant operators, engineers, customers, and stakeholders.

You understand the underlying problem.

You separate customer requests from actual product requirements.

You identify edge cases and unresolved decisions.

You write a product specification that clearly explains the intended behavior, workflows, system states, requirements, and open questions.

You work with Product Design to turn that specification into a strong interface.

You incorporate feedback, resolve ambiguity, and keep the feature moving until the capability works as intended.

The Head of Product provides direction and reviews the most important decisions—but does not need to personally produce every artifact or manage every follow-up.

Early Expectations

Within the first few weeks, you should begin contributing directly to product specifications.

Initially, you may draft sections of specifications or own smaller, well-bounded capabilities with guidance from the Head of Product.

As your understanding of Legion, its operators, and the technical architecture grows, you will rapidly take ownership of larger features.

We are not looking for someone who spends six months observing before contributing.

The Person We’re Looking For

You are an excellent writer.

You can take a complicated conversation and turn it into a clear product definition.

You have strong product judgment and are comfortable making reasonable decisions when requirements are incomplete.

You understand that a customer request is not automatically a product requirement.

You are technically curious and capable of participating meaningfully in discussions with software engineers, systems engineers, operators, and external partners.

You naturally ask questions like:

• 
What problem are we actually trying to solve?

•

About the role

At Riverlane, our mission is to make it possible for anyone to write and run fault-tolerant programs on a quantum computer. A key part of that mission is Deltakit, our open-source, user-facing platform for building, simulating and interpreting QEC experiments. As a Senior Software Engineer, you will own and lead the development of Deltakit, shaping its direction and ensuring it evolves to meet the needs of a growing and highly technical user community.

This role sits at the intersection of research and engineering. You will take cutting-edge ideas from the forefront of QEC and turn them into robust, intuitive software that researchers can rely on. Day to day, this means driving the design and delivery of new features, improving performance and usability, and ensuring the platform scales as adoption grows. You’ll play a key role in planning and prioritising the development roadmap, aligning technical delivery with research milestones, user needs, and broader organisational goals, as well as defining technical direction, making architectural decisions, and setting the standard for high-quality, well-engineered code.

You will also be closely connected to the people who use what we build. By engaging with researchers, engineers and the wider QEC community, you’ll help support adoption of Deltakit, understand how it’s being used in practice, and translate real-world feedback into meaningful improvements. You’ll also play a key role in planning and prioritising the development roadmap, aligning technical delivery with research milestones, user needs, and broader organisational goals. Through this, you’ll ensure the software not only reflects the latest research, but is accessible, reliable and impactful.

Riverlane operates at the forefront of a fast-moving and evolving field. You’ll work as part of a collaborative, multidisciplinary team where ideas are shared openly and learning is continuous. As priorities shift and the technology develops, you’ll help guide the platform forward through both technical leadership and thoughtful planning, bringing clarity, direction and momentum to complex challenges, and playing a central role in advancing Riverlane’s leadership in QEC software.

 

What you will do

  • Lead significant parts of both the internal and external software stack for error-corrected quantum computing systems  
  • Turn internal tools into external and public ones. Own the complete software cycle process: design, development, testing, builds, workflows, releases
  • Mentor, guide and lead engineers in the team
  • Lead collaboration with other engineering teams to integrate their software and hardware artifacts with Deltakit
  • Engage with the community of users and researchers to identify needs and formulate adequate response
  • Contribute actively to open-source projects and lead the Deltakit open-source community
  • Organise and run workshops and tutorials for the community of users

 

What we need

We are considering a range of experience and are therefore advertising this role at different levels of seniority.  Please apply to the role you feel best suits your skills and experience.

  • Strong technical foundation (e.g. computer science, mathematics, physics or similar)
  • Experience designing and building high-quality scientific or technical software, primarily in Python
  • Ability to translate complex, research-driven concepts into robust, scalable and user-friendly solutions
  • Broad understanding of software systems (e.g. compilers, operating systems, computer architecture)
  • Experience shipping software to users and maintaining high engineering standards
  • Curiosity and a strong drive to learn and solve complex problems
  • Collaborative mindset, with experience working across diverse teams
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Ability to shape technical direction, drive best practices, and support others through mentorship and leadership
  • Interest in contributing to the quantum open-source ecosystem

 

Even better if you have

  • Experience with a strongly typed language (e.g. C++ or Rust)

 

What you can expect from us 

  • A comprehensive benefits package that includes an annual bonus plan, private medical insurance, life insurance, and a contributory pension scheme
  • Equity, so that our team can share in the long-term success of Riverlane
  • 28 days annual leave, plus bank holidays and enhanced family leave
  • A diverse work environment that brings together experts in many fields (including software and hardware development, quantum information theory, physics and maths) and over 20 different nationalities
  • A learning environment that encourages individual, team and company growth and development, including a regular programme of learning events and training and conference budgets

 

How to apply

We review CVs as we receive them and interview as soon as we have applications that look like a good match. We do not use closing dates. So, please apply as soon as possible to avoid missing out on this role.

jobs.title: Product Associate
jobs.description:
About Abound

We’re redefining consumer lending in the UK, and beyond. Using advanced AI and Open Banking data, we make fair, affordable personal finance available to more people. While traditional lenders rely almost entirely on credit scores, we look at the full financial picture - how much you spend, and what you can afford to repay to build a deeper, more accurate understanding of each customer's unique financial situation.

And we've shown it works at scale. We’ve issued over £1.3bn in loans directly to customers while delivering market-leading credit performance - for every 10 defaults the industry expects, we see only 3. We also reached profitability just 2.5 years after launch.

Backed by £2bn+ of funding from top-tier investors including Citi, GSR Ventures, and Deutsche Bank, we’re recognised as one of Europe’s fastest-growing fintechs (Sifted, CNBC). Now, we’re expanding into new markets and product lines - and we’re looking for ambitious people who want to learn fast, take ownership, and grow with us.

About the role

We're expanding access to affordable credit by launching credit products that make a real difference to customers. We move quickly, often with leading fintech, consumer and e-commerce companies, so that we can offer affordable credit at the right point in the customer journey. We work in a highly regulated environment, so our products have to work end to end from day one: technically, operationally and commercially.

As a Product Associate, you'll work across product, data and commercials. You'll dig into how our products perform, from funnel conversion to loan-level unit economics, and turn what you find into ideas for how we scale, improve margins and grow. You'll work hands-on with data and code, alongside Product Managers, Engineering, Credit and Operations. You'll help decide where the product goes next, as well as how we ship it.

This role is for top-tier STEM or Economics graduates who think like analysts, build like engineers and care about the P&L like owners, and who want to progress to Product Manager at a fast-growing, industry-leading fintech.

What you'll be doing

Product analytics & insight

• 
Own analysis of product performance across the full funnel: traffic, applications, approvals, conversion, originations, repayment and credit outcomes

• 
Build and maintain the dashboards, metrics and data models that Product, Credit and Operations rely on

• 
Form sharp hypotheses, design experiments (journey changes, pricing, A/B tests) and measure the impact rigorously

• 
Get to the root cause of anomalies quickly, whether the cause is in the data, the code or the customer journey

Unit economics & commercial thinking

• 
Model the economics of each product: acquisition cost, approval and take-up rates, pricing, funding cost, expected loss, servicing cost and lifetime value

• 
Put numbers on the trade-offs behind product decisions, such as wider approval versus higher losses, or partner revenue share versus volume

• 
Track contribution margin and cohort profitability by product, channel and partner, and show where we make or lose money

Growth & product strategy

• 
Come up with ideas for scaling and growing from where we are today (new segments, channels, products and pricing) and estimate what each one is worth

• 
Look across our products and partnerships for places where they reinforce each other: cross-sell, top-ups, repeat lending, shared customers and shared data

• 
Help evaluate new partner opportunities and build the business case, covering volume, economics, integration effort and risk

• 
Turn the strongest ideas into clear proposals and see them through to launch

Building & shipping

• 
Use AI coding tools to build and ship product end to end, across both front-end and back-end, from quick prototypes to features that go live

• 
Build internal tools, automations and data workflows that remove manual work and help the team move faster

• 
Be proficient with our analytics stack: build dashboards in AWS QuickSight and track funnels, events and experiments in PostHog

• 
Use SQL and Python every day to pull, model and analyse data

• 
Learn how our APIs, decisioning flows and data pipelines work, and work directly with engineers on specs, testing and release validation

• 
Support Product Managers with discovery, delivery and partner onboarding

Launch readiness & operations

• 
Define success criteria for each launch and the metrics that show whether it's working

• 
Design test scenarios, including edge cases and failure modes, and test the end-to-end customer journey before release

• 
Work closely with QA to make sure production releases are stable

• 
Monitor production performance after release, and pick up and triage related bugs with engineering

• 
Make sure new products and journeys work at launch for customer support, collections and complaints teams

• 
Use operational data to spot recurring issues, fix them at the source and make sure they're closed out, not just discussed

Who you are

• 
A top-tier STEM or Economics graduate (computer science, engineering, mathematics, physics, economics or similar)

• 
0–2 years of experience, including internships, placements or early-career roles with real responsibility

• 
Strongly analytical and confident with SQL and Python, able to go from raw data to a clear recommendation

• 
Able to build with AI. You use AI coding tools (e.g. Claude Code, Cursor) to ship working front-end and back-end code, and you've built things, whether side projects, hackathons, internal tools or production apps

• 
Hands-on with analytics tools such as AWS QuickSight, PostHog or similar BI and product analytics platforms

• 
Commercially minded. You naturally ask how something makes money, and you enjoy modelling unit economics, pricing and P&L

• 
Strong product sense. You have opinions on the products you use, why they work and how they could grow

• 
A structured problem-solver who can break down messy, real-world problems

• 
A clear communicator who can walk an engineer through a model and make a recommendation to leadership

Nice to have: an interest in consumer credit, lending, payments or fintech; experience with experimentation and statistics.

How you work (and what we value)

• 
You think like an owner, of both the customer outcome and the commercial outcome

• 
You'd rather build a quick prototype or run the numbers than debate in the abstract

• 
You follow through until problems are actually solved

• 
You're comfortable with ambiguity and don't wait for perfect instructions

• 
You speak up when something doesn't make sense, and you help fix it

• 
You put in extra effort at key moments, such as launches and live incidents, knowing that's where the real learning happens

Progression & growth

This role is a stepping stone to Product Management, with a clear progression path. As a Product Associate, you'll be expected to:

• 
Build deep knowledge of our products, data and commercials

• 
Consistently own problems end to end and deliver measurable business and customer impact

• 
Show strong judgement, data-driven thinking and stakeholder management

High performers will progress to Junior Product Manager as they begin to:

• 
Own a product area or metric independently, including its commercial performance

• 
Lead defined workstreams within launches or partner integrations

• 
Originate growth ideas that make it onto the roadmap and deliver results

Progression is based on impact and ownership, not time served.

What we offer

• 
Everyone owns a piece of the company: equity

• 
Hybrid working, with 3 days a week in the office

• 
25 days' holiday a year, plus 8 bank holidays

• 
2 paid volunteering days per year

• 
One month's paid sabbatical after 4 years

• 
Employee loan

• 
Free gym membership

• 
Team wellness budget to be active together: set up a yoga class, a tennis lesson or go bouldering

Now, we’re expanding into new markets and product lines - and we’re looking for ambitious people who want to learn fast, take ownership, and grow with us.

The Role

We are hiring a Product Lead to own our Express / Mid-prime personal loan product, one of our highest-priority growth areas. This is unsecured personal lending in the higher-APR mid-prime space (30% to 50% APR), with loans typically from £2,000 to £10,000, and customers acquired primarily through price-comparison and aggregator marketplaces. Our ambition is to grow this product many times over while improving its economics, and this role owns the product that makes that happen.

This is a product role first. You will own the Express/Mid-prime proposition end to end: who we serve, how we quote and present offers on marketplaces, how the journey converts, how we price, and how the product performs once the loans are on the book. What makes it different from a typical product role is that the product is credit. The levers that drive growth, such as eligibility, pricing, offer design and underwriting, are the same levers that drive loss rates, so you need to be comfortable working with risk and data science rather than handing that part off.

We think this is a great role for someone with around four to five years of experience who has built a strong foundation in lending or fintech, has worked hands-on with data and credit decisioning, and is ready to own a product outright rather than a slice of one. You will set the direction for the segment, run the roadmap, and be accountable for the results, with the backing of experienced risk, data science and commercial leaders around you.

Our decisioning is built on Open Banking and cashflow underwriting rather than credit scores alone. For a higher-APR population acquired through marketplaces, seeing real affordability is what lets us select and price better than the market. The interesting product problem is that richer data comes at a cost to conversion, so the job is to capture that data advantage while designing a journey and offer that customers actually complete.

The defining challenge is balance: scaling volume by an order of magnitude while building a book of genuinely good credit quality. The best people in this space know that those two goals can be reconciled rather than traded off, and are curious enough to work out how.

• 
Own conversion through the journey, from quote to disbursal, including how we ask customers for Open Banking data and how that affects drop-off and the quality of the book.

• 
Understand and actively manage adverse selection in marketplace-acquired lending, shaping offer, pricing and decisioning strategy to attract the customers we want and screen out the risk we do not.

• 
Work with data science to make sure our credit models are calibrated and tuned for this population rather than inherited unchanged from prime or adjacent segments, and be able to get into the data yourself when needed.

• 
Use credit and commercial insight to optimise unit economics, balancing approval rates, pricing, loss rates and volume so the product scales profitably.

• 
Monitor product and portfolio performance across the customer lifecycle, spotting emerging trends, risks and opportunities early.

• 
Shape underwriting strategy, segmentation, credit policy and decisioning logic in partnership with risk and data science.

• 
Design and evaluate experiments and strategy changes, and turn the analysis into clear, actionable recommendations.

• 
Own the management information for the segment: define the metrics, monitoring and reporting that let the business make consistent decisions about the product.

• 
Assess new initiatives, customer segments and product changes with both a commercial and a credit lens.

• 
Present clear, structured updates on product performance to senior leadership and governance forums, and support funding and due diligence conversations where the product is in focus.

Who you are

• 
A product person at heart: you care about the customer, the journey and the commercial outcome, and you want to own something end to end.

• 
Quantitative and hands-on. You are comfortable in SQL and Python (or similar), you can interrogate a dataset yourself, and you can hold your own in a conversation with data scientists about model performance and calibration.

• 
Credit-literate. You understand how eligibility, pricing and underwriting decisions shape the book you end up with, and you have a working understanding of adverse selection and why it matters in marketplace lending.

• 
Commercially sharp, with a solid grasp of unit economics and a clear understanding that product decisions in lending have to work for both growth and portfolio performance.

• 
Curious about trade-offs rather than defensive about them: alert to the fact that deeper affordability assessment can hurt conversion, and motivated by the challenge of capturing its value without sacrificing growth.

• 
Able to move between detail and direction: happy getting into the data on a Tuesday and shaping the roadmap on a Wednesday.

• 
Confident challenging assumptions and turning analysis into practical action, and able to explain your reasoning clearly to people who are not analysts.

• 
Collaborative and credible with risk, commercial, engineering and data science teams.

• 
Structured, proactive and comfortable in a scaling environment where priorities evolve quickly and ownership is expected.

Experience and background

• 
Around four to five years of experience in product, credit strategy, analytics or a closely related role within consumer lending or fintech. We are deliberately targeting this level: this is a step-up role for someone ready to own a product, not a lateral move for someone who has run several.

• 
Experience in unsecured consumer lending, ideally Unsecured Personal Loans (UPL), with exposure to the mechanics of acquiring customers through price-comparison or aggregator marketplaces. Direct experience in higher-APR or near-prime lending is a strong plus but not a prerequisite.

• 
Hands-on data skills: SQL as a minimum, and ideally Python or R for analysis. You do not need to be a data scientist, but you need to be able to work alongside them as a peer and do your own analysis.

Experience working with or alongside credit decisioning, scorecards or risk models, and an understanding of how they are built, monitored and adjusted for a specific population.

Some experience of pricing, eligibility or offer design, and of using experiments or A/B tests to evaluate changes.

Proven track record of designing DoEs and executing structured experiments

• 
Experience applying statistical process control, yield improvement and throughput optimisation in production

Excellent teamwork, documentation and communication skills

Nice to Have

Experience transferring processes to contract manufacturers or foundries

Failure analysis experience

Patent or IP contributions

Analyze failure modes (leakage, contamination, cavitation, fluid hammer) and define mitigation strategies and design margins.

Correlate test data against predictive models and update margins/requirements accordingly.

Interface across design, test, and operations functions throughout the vehicle lifecycle.

jobs.title: Project Manager - Integrations
jobs.description:
Company Description

We’re Checkout.com. You might not know our name, but companies like eBay, Spotify, Klarna, Uber, and Sony do, because we’re behind many of the digital experiences you use every day. 

We are where the world checks out, enabling over 10 billion transactions yearly for more than one billion global shoppers. 

Whether you want to book a holiday, order food, renew a subscription, or check out online, there’s a good chance our tech powers the payments behind the scenes. Our platform helps the most ambitious businesses deliver effortless digital experiences, at scale. 

If you want to do career-defining work, you’ve come to the right place. We move fast, think globally, and believe great teams are built by hiring exceptional people with conviction, curiosity, and the desire to make an impact. 

With 20 offices across six continents and London as our HQ, we’re shaping the future of fintech – and we’re just getting started.

Join us at ProcessOut

ProcessOut is a pioneer in the payment orchestration space. We are on a mission to help merchants build, scale and optimize their payment infrastructure. We work to bring simplicity, flexibility & performance to payments.

Millions of transactions are routed via ProcessOut everyday for merchants all over the world. We are proud to partner with amazing merchants like Glovo, Bolt, Sainsbury’s, Dott, Hellofresh and many more!

We were acquired by Checkout.com in 2020 with the goal of growing our global reach.

If you are looking to join a very fast-moving company with passionate, hard-working & fun teams, ProcessOut is for you! At ProcessOut, we are looking for people who are convinced they can play a central part in the Company's success! We are looking for people who are passionate, who are looking to achieve their full potential & who will actively contribute to strengthen the links between our teams. We value people that fully own their work and are passionate about building the next generation of online payments with us.

Project Management at ProcessOut

As a Mid-level Project Manager within our Integrations Team, you will sit at the heart of our merchants expansion. The team is dedicated to:

• 
Architecting payments framework that guarantee high velocity and uncompromising quality for new payment providers on-boarding.

• 
Integrating with a global network of payment providers.

In this high-impact role, your key responsibilities will include:

• 
Own the planification of a team of 10+ engineers, which will involve collecting the needs from merchants

• 
Orchestrating complex merchant timelines and delivery projects, championing excellence at every stage.

• 
Cultivating and maintaining strategic partnerships with global payment providers (we have more than 100, but only few are strategical)

We operate as a self-sufficient, fully agile unit. To thrive here, you should:

• 
Possess a deep understanding of both payment ecosystems and engineering principles.

• 
You'll collaborate with Europe's leading merchants, work alongside world-class engineers and discuss with banks from all around the world

• 
Masterfully navigate complex trade-offs and rapid context switching in a dynamic environment.

• 
Drive external communication and engage directly, with often physical visits, with partners across Europe.

• 
Being able to challenge other remits (engineering, product, merchants, providers) with data driven decisions

We are experiencing constant growth in the number of transactions handled, new clients, and integrations. That’s why we pay very close attention to efficiency and we are happy to improve our processes.

About you

• 
At least 5 years of experience in payments

• 
Know your way around web-related tech (HTTP, TLS, proxies, API conventions...)

• 
Have a technical background and is able to understand software code

• 
Able to communicate with third-party providers from both a technical perspective and business

• 
Be product minded

• 
Always curious and passionate about understanding the business

Nice to have

• 
French language

• 
Cards payments knowledge

What you will be doing

• 
Working with engineers, merchants and payments providers to connect ProcessOut to worldwide acquirers and payment methods

• 
Contributing to the business by computing KPIs and improving our processes in order to improve them

• 
Own the product vision to help on designing, building, and releasing new features

If you don't meet all the requirements but think you might still be right for the role, please apply anyway. We're always keen to speak to people who connect with our mission and values.

Additional Information

Bring all of you to work

We create the conditions for high performers to thrive, through real ownership, fewer blockers, and work that makes a difference from day one.

Here, you’ll move fast, take on meaningful challenges, and be recognized for the impact you deliver. It’s a place where ambition gets met with opportunity, and where your growth is in your hands.

We work as one team, and we back each other to succeed. So whatever your background or identity, if you’re ready to grow and make a difference, you’ll be right at home here.

It’s important we set you up for success and make our process as accessible as possible. So let us know in your application, or tell your recruiter directly, if you need anything to make your experience or working environment more comfortable.

Life at Checkout.com

We understand that work is just one part of your life. Our hybrid working model offers flexibility, with three days per week in the office to support collaboration and connection.

Curious about what it’s like to be part of our team? Visit our Careers Page to learn more about our culture, open roles, and what drives us.

jobs.description:
You want to help build Europe’s resilience? You want to protect people and critical infrastructure – ultimately saving the lives of thousands?

You want to work at the frontier of high-performance autonomous systems?

Join us at CDDS to bring next-generation of control, state-estimation and computer cision algorithms into high-speed kinetic interceptor drones.

CDDS specializes in developing low-collateral kinetic interceptors designed to neutralize malicious drones (Mavics, FPV racers and fast fixed wings). Our solutions are built for precision and safety, minimizing risk to surroundings while effectively countering unauthorized or threatening unmanned aerial systems. We work at the cutting edge of counter-drone technology, delivering reliable protection for critical assets and environments.

Tasks

Your Mission

We are looking for an exceptional Control & Flight Test Engineer to drive the control, vision, hardware and operational stack of our interceptor drone platform to the next level. You will test, tune and develop state-estimation, control and vision algorithms that directly determine successful target interception. You will act as the eyes and ears of the R&D team on customer demos and field tests abroad. You will gain a big insights in all our systems as you have to make sure that they are working such that it can be deployed to a user.

You will work closely with all teams, meaning control, vison, software and hardware experts — ensuring your and the teams algorithms translate directly into field performance.

Core Responsibilities

• 
Designing and validate low-latency guidance and control strategies

• 
Help to push our multi-sensor fusion algorithms for state estimation

• 
Verify and test new computer vision approaches

• 
Test and Validate Low-Level Control Software and Hardware Changes

• 
Raise risks and issues you see on the field to the R&D team

• 
Analyse data, evaluate performance and failure modes of our full tactical unit while doing intercepts

Requirements

We are looking for people who thrive on mathematical depth, rapid iteration, and hands-on flight testing. You take full ownership of field test — Aligning with the R&D team and your Safety Pilot.

Your Profile

• 
PhD or MSc in Robotics, Control Engineering, Electrical Engineering or similar field with strong academic record (from ETH Zürich or equivalent)

• 
Strong analytical mindset with the ability to derive, evaluate, and validate a complex system

• 
Good understanding of classical & optimal control, Kalman filtering, state estimation, and linear algebra (rotations and transformations in SE(3))

• 
Proficiency in Python and Linux

• 
Comfortable in fast-paced, high-ownership environments with long hours when the mission demands it

• 
Openness to travel often

Nice-to-Have

• 
ROS2, PX4, Ardupilot and real-time robotics software

• 
Fast-moving object interception / high-dynamics control

• 
Experience with Simulation Frameworks like Gazebo or Isaac Sim

• 
Background in drone flight testing or competitive robotics

Benefits

Why CDDS

• 
Direct impact on a mission‑critical technology shaping Europe’s security landscape

• 
Fast‑moving startup environment with high ownership

• 
Work with a highly technical, ambitious, and hands‑on team

• 
Real‑world testing, deployments, and customer demonstrations

• 
Attractive compensation

Details

jobs.description:
PEAX bietet eine Lösung für automatisierten Dokumenteneingang, intelligentes Document Processing und Weiterverarbeitung in nachgelagerten Geschäftsprozessen. Damit werden unsere Kunden von administrativem Aufwand befreit und erkennen den Wert ihrer Daten. Wir suchen Menschen, die unsere Produktentwicklung mit analytischer Tiefe und einem ausgeprägten AI-First-Mindset auf das nächste Level bringen.

Aufgaben

Das bewegst du

• Du verantwortest das fachliche Herz unseres Produkts: das Domänenmodell. Capabilities, Business Objects, Business Rules und Prozesse hältst du korrekt, widerspruchsfrei und aktuell. Und du sorgst dafür, dass sie über Domänen hinweg zusammenpassen. 

• Aus vielschichtigen, oft widersprüchlichen Anforderungen machst du klare Struktur: Nachvollziehbare Use Cases, scharf geschnittene Anforderungen und eindeutige Akzeptanzkriterien. Dein wichtigster Beitrag ist dabei nicht, jeden Einzelwunsch zu spezifizieren. Es ist zu erkennen, wann mehrere Einzelfälle dasselbe allgemeine Problem sind, und die allgemeine Lösung durchzusetzen. 

• Du präzisierst Produktentscheide für die Umsetzung: Regeln, Grenzfälle, Zustände und Sollverhalten. Bei komplexen und domänenübergreifenden Themen führst du die Spezifikation selbst. Im Übrigen setzt du den Standard, nach dem im Team spezifiziert wird, und entwickelst die Modellierungskompetenz deiner Kolleg:innen weiter. 

• Qualität ist für dich Teil der Spezifikationsarbeit und kein nachgelagerter Schritt. Du erstellst E2E-Testkonzepte und Testfälle für deinen Bereich und prüfst Features. Wir sind ein kleines Team, in dem alle die Qualität des Produkts mittragen. 

• Du bist für die von dir verantworteten Features die fachliche Ansprechperson für Engineering, Design, Customer Success und Sales sowie für Partner, Reseller und Kunden. Du bist auch die Person, die „so geht das fachlich nicht“ sagen kann und dafür gehört wird. 

• Deine Arbeit startet in der Product Discovery: Bei der Problemrahmung, nicht erst bei der Übersetzung fertiger Entscheide. Zudem bringst du deine fachliche Sicht in Architekturentscheide ein, wo sie Konsequenzen für das Domänenmodell haben. 

• PEAX baut gerade agentische Architekturen. Du nutzt AI-Tools strukturiert und verantwortungsvoll als Bestandteil unseres Requirement Engineering Prozesses.

Qualifikation

Das bringst du mit

• Mehrjährige Senior-Erfahrung als Requirements Engineer, Business Analyst oder in einer vergleichbaren Rolle im B2B-SaaS-Produktumfeld, idealerweise in einer Scale-up-Phase und mit Hintergrund in Document Management, ECM, Workflow-Automatisierung oder einem verwandten Information-Hub-Umfeld. Du hast dabei nachweisbar Verantwortung für fachliche Modelle getragen und nicht nur für Spezifikationsdokumente. 

• Ausbildungshintergrund in Wirtschaftsinformatik, Informatik, Business Engineering, BWL mit IT-Affinität (FH, Universität). MSc-Niveau ideal, Bachelor mit entsprechender Senior-Erfahrung ebenfalls möglich. 

• Echte Modellierungstiefe: Du kannst ein Geschäftsproblem in Entitäten, Zustände, Regeln und Prozesse zerlegen, so dass das Ergebnis widerspruchsfrei ist. Du formulierst Akzeptanzkriterien so, dass sie prüfbar sind. Sicherer Umgang mit BPMN, UML, Use Cases und User Stories sowie mit Jira und Confluence. Kenntnisse in ArchiMate sind ein Pluspunkt. 

• Generalisierungsinstinkt: Du erkennst, wann mehrere Einzelfälle dasselbe allgemeine Problem sind, und setzt die allgemeine Lösung durch. Du fragst nach dem Problem, bevor du nach der Lösung fragst, und du kannst eine Anforderung auch ablehnen. 

• Eingehendes Verständnis für administrative Prozesse in KMU, die Aufbereitung von Daten und zur Verfügungstellung via Schnittstellen an Drittanwendungen. Damit zusammenhängend die Fähigkeit, Problemstellen in bestehenden Prozessen zu analysieren und durch intelligente Abläufe zu ersetzen. 

• Hohe Affinität zu AI-Tools, idealerweise erste Erfahrung mit AI-gestützter Spezifikationsarbeit, Prompt Engineering oder agentischen Systemen aus Produkt-Sicht. 

• Deutsch auf Muttersprach-Niveau, Englisch verhandlungssicher (C1). Sicheres Auftreten auf C-Level.

Benefits

Wir bieten dir 

• Faire Spesenregelung 

• Förderung und Unterstützung zur Weiterentwicklung und Weiterbildung 

• PEAX Private Abo 

• Flache Hierarchien, agile Arbeitsweise 

• Flexible Arbeitszeiten und Homeoffice; Standort in Luzern (Hybrid) 

• Tolles Office und Begegnungsort inmitten der Stadt Luzern

jobs.title: Founding Marketing Manager
jobs.description:
Important: this role is based in our offices in Chiasso, Switzerland, and is open to EU citizens only.

About Anthropos

Anthropos is the Enterprise AI transformation platform. We help companies map, verify, and develop the skills of their workforce with AI Simulations, AI Labs, AI Interviews, and our AI Academy. Enterprises in energy, transportation, and technology use us to answer a question no HR system can: what can our people actually do, and are they ready for AI?

We are a global team that has been building in the skills and assessment space for more than a decade. Most of us built and scaled a previous company in this exact market to a successful exit. Now we are doing it again, with AI at the core.

The role

You will be our first marketing hire, and you will own marketing.

There is no playbook to inherit and no team to delegate to on day one. You will work side by side with our CEO and founder and with the sales team, from our offices in Chiasso, and your job is to build the machine that grows our pipeline, our brand, and ultimately our revenue.

This is an operator role, not a strategy-only role. You will write the copy, ship the campaign, run the event, look at the data, and decide what to do next. If that excites you more than managing an agency, keep reading.

What you'll do

• Demand generation. Design and run campaigns that put qualified enterprise buyers (CHROs, HR and Engineering leaders, CTOs) in front of our sales team. You own the pipeline number with them.

• SEO and GEO. Grow our organic presence on search engines and inside AI assistants (ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity). Being found by AI is as important to us as being found by Google, and we are early enough that you can win here.

• Events. Plan and run our presence at conferences, executive dinners, and our own events, end to end: pick them, organize them, work the room, follow up.

• Content and brand. Shape how Anthropos sounds and looks in public: website, blog, LinkedIn, email, sales materials. Make the brand feel as good as the product.

• Measurement. Instrument what you do, report on what worked, kill what didn't, and double down fast.

• Structure. As things start working, turn them into repeatable processes and eventually into a team you help build.

Who you are

• An entrepreneur at heart who knows marketing. You treat the function like your own business: you spot opportunities, act without waiting for permission, and own the outcome. Behind that instinct is real experience: years of generalist marketing in startups across demand gen, content, events, and product marketing, so you know which levers actually move pipeline.

• Someone who gets things done. You are extremely operational. You default to doing, not briefing someone else to do, and you bring results fast. You like being measured on them.

• An expert with Claude Code, or a heavy daily user of it. We use AI in a very advanced way across the whole company, and we expect marketing to work the same way: producing at a pace and volume a traditional marketer can't match. This is a real requirement, not a nice-to-have.

• Confident in a startup that moves very fast. We change direction quickly, the bar is high, and some days are stressful. In exchange, you will learn more in a year here than in five anywhere else. You need to genuinely want that trade.

• A big risk-taker. You launch things that might fail, test channels nobody assigned you, and own the result either way.

• Not looking for a nine-to-five. This is a startup job, and we are honest about what that means: we work quite a lot. If what you want is a predictable 9-to-5, this is not the right fit, and that's okay. If you want the intensity because of what you get to build, own, and learn, you will feel at home.

• Fluent in written and spoken English, at a near-perfect level. Most of what you produce will be read by an international audience. Italian is a plus.

• An EU citizen. Hiring non-EU citizens in Switzerland requires more time and we cannot currently afford that.

• Able to work from our offices in Chiasso, Ticino. We work in person, with one remote day per week (Thursdays). You need to live in, or be ready to move to, an area where you can commute to Chiasso every day: the provinces of Como, Milan or Varese (Italy), or Switzerland. Relocation support is available where possible.

Not an EU citizen, but sure you are the right person for this role? Write to us before you apply, at ----- and tell us why. We will consider strong candidates.

What you'll get

• CHF 42,000–50,000 per year, plus a very generous stock package. We'd rather be upfront: this is a startup salary paired with real ownership in the company, and the upside grows with the business you help build.

• Relocation support, where available, if you are not already in the area.

• The ability to grow very fast. You start as our first marketing hire; if you deliver, you build and lead the function. No queue of people ahead of you.

• A direct working relationship with the founder and the sales team: short feedback loops, no layers.

• The tools to work like it's the AI era: Claude Code, our own platform, and budget for what you need.

How we hire

We use our own product. The process: apply → complete an AI Simulation built for this role → meet the team → offer. It is fast, and you will experience exactly what we sell.

jobs.title: Energy Data Engineer & Developer
jobs.description:
Drive the energy transition by providing sustainable technological solutions through our digital platform, facilitating from planning to contract tendering to implementation of renewable energy systems in real estate and industrial companies. We enable our customers to increase the economic efficiency and CO2 balance of their properties while minimizing technical, commercial, and energy risks.

To strengthen our Product Management team, we are looking for an Energy Data Analyst & Developer who will contribute to the analysis of energy data, support the development of AI-based price and energy forecasts, and generate actionable insights through the analysis of operational and financial performance. Join this energy revolution and help us transform energy supply in a sustainable and economically viable way!

Tasks

• Analyze energy data, including production, consumption, and storage information to identify optimization opportunities

• Conduct AI-based market analysis and contribute to the development of price and energy forecasts

• Analyze asset data, project progress and operational, environmental as well as financial performance

• Perform trend, variance and gap analysis, translating findings into actionable recommendations

• Validate data quality and perform plausibility checks to continuously improve analytical outputs

• Develop and maintain a central data and reporting infrastructure in close collaboration with IT teams

• Create KPI reports, dashboards, and data visualizations for internal and external stakeholders

• Collaborate closely with management, operations, sales, and country organizations to support data-driven decision-making

Requirements

• Completed degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Science, Business Informatics, Physics, Engineering or a related field — or equivalent practical experience

• 3+ years building data pipelines that ran in production, with real users and real consequences when they broke — not proofs of concept

• High proficiency in SQL, including window functions and time-series aggregation, and strong Python

• Experience operating a time-series or analytical data store — TimescaleDB, PostgreSQL at scale, ClickHouse, Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks or comparable

• Practical experience deploying and maintaining your own infrastructure: infrastructure-as-code (Terraform or similar), CI/CD, containers, cloud 

• You have been on the hook when a pipeline failed, and can describe what you changed afterwards

• Comfortable being the sole owner of a system — you will have a team around you, but nobody will be assigning you tickets for the parts you own

Benefits

• An attractive salary package and exciting development opportunities

• Further training in renewable energies and project management

• A dynamic, innovative environment with short decision-making processes and plenty of creative freedom

• The opportunity to play an active role in the energy transition and make a real impact
